articles.title: NFL Week 9: The Rams get a much-needed defensive boost, plus Bears hold on
articles.summary: Week 9 of the NFL season featured a Super Bowl favorite finally getting over .500, some magic from Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders and a bounce-back performance from an MVP candidate.
articles.body: Week 9 of the NFL season featured a Super Bowl favorite finally getting over .500, some magic from Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders and a bounce-back performance from an MVP candidate. Here’s everything you need to know from Sunday. Welcome back, Myles Garrett. So long, Puka Nacua? Garrett, the reigning defensive player of the year whom the Los Angeles Rams traded for in the offseason, returned from a knee injury that had sidelined him for seven games and made his presence felt immediately in a 20-13 win over Washington (2-5-1). All three of his tackles ended in sacks, and his first sack also forced a fumble to help the Rams (5-4) climb above .500 for the first time. How impactful was Garrett? In eight previous games, the Rams had 12 sacks combined. It was the first game Garrett played alongside Aaron Donald, the superstar defensive tackle who came out of retirement to create an all-world defensive line. The Rams might not be able to celebrate for long. On their final play of the game, star receiver Puka Nacua suffered a reported knee injury that will require more imaging Monday to determine its severity. Nacua was targeted 19 times, and he finished with 14 receptions for 150 yards and a touchdown. He did not discuss his injury with reporters after the game, and he was visibly in a good mood. Another Commanders game ended with a head-scratching final play. With the ball on the Rams’ 31-yard line, Washington threw a short pass, then tried an unsuccessful lateral until the clock ran out. Why not try a deep pass into the end zone? Coach Dan Quinn said Washington called in two plays — one a deep ball and the other a short completion and lateral option if the Rams blitzed hard. “Didn’t love our execution at the end,” he said. Bears survive five turnovers The worst record in the NFC North belongs to 6-3 Green Bay. In a division that difficult, a team’s margin for error to make the playoffs is razor thin, which is why the Chicago Bears (7-2) must be one of the most relieved teams in the league after Week 9. After having led Tampa Bay 14-0, Chicago proceeded to turn the ball over five times — four interceptions by Caleb Williams and a fumble inside its own 20-yard line by receiver Luther Burden III with 3:48 to play and Tampa Bay (3-6) trailing by eight. The Buccaneers would score a touchdown and a 2-point conversion for a tie. Yet for all of Williams’ erratic play, his 38-yard completion in the final minute all but sealed the win by putting Chicago within range of a 38-yard field goal that Cairo Santos drilled for a walk-off 27-24 victory. Tampa Bay quarterback Baker Mayfield added two interceptions. The six interceptions were the most combined by two quarterbacks in a game this season. Chicago is the first team to win a game while turning the ball over five-plus times since 2006. The Chiefs end their two-game losing streak For years, as Patrick Mahomes played, so went Kansas City. But it might be more accurate this season to say running back Kenneth Walker III is the barometer for the Chiefs’ offense. Kansas City (6-2) ended its two-game losing streak in a 35-12 rout of the New York Jets (2-7) in which Walker bounced back with 102 rushing yards and a touchdown on the ground and 41 yards with two touchdown catches through the air. He had been held to just 3.0 yards per carry in his previous two games, both Chiefs losses. Walker averaged nearly double that (5.6 yards) Sunday. Mahomes looked like he would be leaving the game in the second quarter after his arm bent awkwardly when he was sandwiched by multiple defenders. Instead, he finished with 242 yards and two touchdowns. Shedeur Sanders runs out of magic in overtime Sanders led two comeback drives in the first start of his sophomore season, but he couldn’t lead the Browns all the way to a win against the New Orleans Saints. Cleveland lost 23-22, but Sanders had some encouraging moments. He completed 19 of 31 passes for 297 yards, the second-highest passing total of his career. With the Browns trailing 16-13 in the fourth quarter, Sanders calmly led a game-tying drive for a field goal despite getting the ball with under a minute to go. After a long drive by the Saints to start overtime, Sanders responded by leading an eight-play, 67-yard touchdown drive. But the Browns went for 2 and the win after the score, and the attempt failed, dropping Cleveland to 5-4. The Giants keep finding a way, remain atop the NFC East After the Giants lost quarterback Jaxson Dart in Week 2, New York’s season looked to be in major trouble. But head coach John Harbaugh has kept the team afloat in his first year at the helm, and the Giants improved to 5-2-1 with a win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday. New York is 4-1-1 since Dart’s injury. On Sunday, starter J.J. McCarthy had to leave the game briefly with an injury, but he returned to close out the Giants’ first win in Philly since 2013. New York is the only team in the NFC East with a winning record, even after the Dallas Cowboys beat the Indianapolis Colts. Raiders’ regression continues; Chargers remain winless Under coach Klint Kubiak and quarterback Kirk Cousins, Las Vegas was one of the season’s early surprises as it started 3-0. In hindsight, those three wins were against subpar competition in the Miami Dolphins, the Los Angeles Chargers and the New Orleans Saints. After Sunday’s 38-17 loss at San Francisco, the Raiders (4-5) have lost five of their last six games. Sunday’s was the sixth consecutive game in which they have allowed 30 or more points, the longest streak in team history. As the losses mount, will Las Vegas finally turn to No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza? And yet for all of that regression from the Raiders, they still are not the AFC West team that feels the worst after nine weeks. After a 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans at home, the Chargers remain the NFL’s last winless team. They join the 2011 Indianapolis Colts as the only teams since 2000 to start a season 0-8 the year after they made the playoffs. The lone consolation for Los Angeles fans is that at least one streak ended. Justin Herbert’s fourth-quarter touchdown pass ended a run of 37 consecutive drives without scoring a touchdown. Herbert has now gone 10 consecutive starts without multiple touchdowns.

articles.title: In 2019, Patrick Mahomes bought a $1.9 million Missouri home; four years later, his family had outgrown the luxury property
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes paid about $1.9 million for a 1950s ranch house in Kansas City in February 2019.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes paid about $1.9 million for a 1950s ranch house in Kansas City in February 2019. Four years later, he and his wife Brittany listed it at $2.9 million. The home sat in the Country Club District, and it was meant to be a settled base after his first season as the Chiefs starter. It became a stop along the way. Two young children, a record contract and bigger plans for Missouri pushed the family toward something larger.Why Patrick Mahomes bought a $1.9 million Missouri home in 2019Mahomes closed on the house in February 2019. He had just finished his first full season as a starter, which ended with an overtime loss to New England in the AFC title game, and he had been named league MVP. The price was reported at roughly $1.9 million. County records did not give an exact figure, and a few outlets put it slightly lower.The house was built in 1953 and sits on about 1.4 acres. Listing coverage described nearly 4,800 square feet, hardwood floors and big walls of glass, a classic mid-century look. Dirt reported that the couple spent around $400,000 on renovations. One of the better-known touches was a custom closet for his sneakers, reported at more than 180 pairs.It was also his first real house. Before it, Mahomes owned a two-bedroom apartment in Kansas City that he bought as a rookie in late 2017. He tried to sell that place in 2019 and could not. So the ranch house was a big step up, but it was never a showpiece by superstar standards. Many outlets called it surprisingly understated. For a 23-year-old with a rookie deal, that was a telling choice. He picked a quiet street over a statement.What changed for the Patrick Mahomes family between 2019 and 2023The pace was hard to follow. In February 2020, the Chiefs won Super Bowl LIV, and Mahomes took the game’s MVP award. Five months later he signed a 10-year, $503 million extension. That same year he bought a Dallas-area home in Westlake, Texas, for $3.37 million, which kept him close to his home state.Then the family grew. Sterling Skye was born in February 2021. Patrick and Brittany married in March 2022. Their son, Patrick Lavon Mahomes III, known as Bronze, arrived that November.By mid-2023, the household looked nothing like it did in 2019. A young player and his girlfriend had become a married couple with two toddlers. Brittany was building her own career, including a co-ownership stake in the Kansas City Current. Mahomes was splitting offseasons between Missouri and Texas. A house bought for the first version of that life was now carrying the second.Nothing about the property was wrong. It was simply sized for an earlier chapter, and that is the quiet reason most athletes sell homes like this one.How the Mahomes home listing played outDirt reported the listing in July 2023 with an asking price of $2.9 million. That was about $1 million above the reported purchase price. The gap is not pure profit. The renovations alone took a large bite, and selling costs would take more. Still, the number shows how much value had gathered around the address, and probably around the name attached to it.The house did not linger. Fox 4 Kansas City later reported that the three-bedroom, three-bathroom home at 1257 W. 57th St. sold to a trust in the name of David Bradley III. Bradley works for the News-Press & Gazette Co., a St. Joseph media company owned by his family. He is also an owner of BERKS Group, a Kansas City family office.The reports I reviewed did not make the final sale price clear, so the public figure that stands is the $2.9 million ask. It is fair to treat that number with some care. Asking prices and closing prices are different things, and the Mahomes camp has not discussed the deal.What is clear is the speed. Compare that with 2019, when his apartment sat unsold. Four years of fame, a Super Bowl ring and a very visible address made this a different kind of listing.Where Patrick Mahomes plans to live nextEarlier in 2023, Mahomes bought land in Cass County, Missouri, south of Kansas City, and began building a custom home with Brittany, according to reports. Coverage has also pointed to a private par-3 golf hole on the property, a nod to his love of the sport. The family has shared little publicly, so the exact size and cost remain unconfirmed.The ranch house was not the only property to go. In July 2023, the same month the ranch house hit the market, he put his Kansas City penthouse near Arrowhead Stadium up for $550,000. Architectural Digest reported that it sold by October.Taken together, the moves read like a clean-out. The properties tied to his early years in Kansas City were cleared as a larger home came online, while the Westlake house stays as the Texas anchor. That is a sensible way to handle a portfolio that grew quickly.The bigger signal is about where he intends to be. Mahomes is signed through 2031, and building from scratch is a long-term bet on Missouri. He is not adapting a smaller home to fit a growing family. He is building around that family instead, and that is a different kind of commitment than the one he made in 2019.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Re-Grading the 10 Biggest NFL Trade Deadline Deals of the Past Decade
articles.summary: As the 2026 NFL trade deadline approaches, it's a good time to look back at the biggest moves from the past decade and how they panned out.
articles.body:
As the 2026 NFL trade deadline approaches, it's a good time to look back at the biggest moves from the past decade and how they panned out.

Excluding this year's blockbuster deals, we've broken down the most buzzworthy pre-deadline moves from 2016 onward, examining the trade details, how teams used the draft capital in these transactions and the impact of the player(s) involved.

Three years is more than enough time to grade these transactions properly, though a few deals are still only a year or two old, so projections of productivity factor into some of the grades.

Here's our review of the biggest trades that sent midseason shockwaves across the NFL over the last 10 years.

Colts Acquire Sauce Gardner from the Jets (2025)

Indianapolis Colts Received: CB Sauce Gardner

New York Jets Received: 2026 first-rounder, 2027 first-rounder, WR Adonai Mitchell

This trade happened a year ago, but it's already aging poorly for the Indianapolis Colts.

The New York Jets shocked many by dealing Sauce Gardner almost four months after signing him to a four-year, $120.4 million extension. In his first two seasons with Gang Green, he earned two first-team All-Pro and two Pro Bowl nods.

Yet you can't blame Jets general manager Darren Mougey for acquiring two first-round picks and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell for Gardner. The Colts overpaid for a player whom they thought would help them make a deep playoff run last season.

Instead, Indianapolis fell apart largely because of injuries. Quarterback Daniel Jones tore his Achilles in December of last year, and Gardner missed four of the Colts' last five games.

In seven games with the Colts this season, Gardner has logged only six pass breakups and has yet to record an interception. He's allowing a passer rating of 96.8 out of a possible 158.3. Gardner has only three career interceptions, but in his rookie year alone, he led the league with 20 pass breakups.

Meanwhile, in 12 games with the Jets, Mitchell has already eclipsed his receiving numbers from his 25-game tenure with the Colts. He's caught 40 passes for 566 yards and three touchdowns with the Jets after hauling in only 32 catches for 464 yards and zero touchdowns in Indianapolis.

The Jets continue to benefit from this deal as the Colts sink to the bottom of the standings. Through Week 8, Indianapolis is in line to send Gang Green the No. 4 overall pick in the 2027 draft.

Cowboys Get Quinnen Williams from the Jets (2025)

Dallas Cowboys Received: DT Quinnen Williams

New York Jets Received: 2026 second-rounder, 2027 first-rounder (higher of Cowboys' first-rounders) and DT Mazi Smith

While the Sauce Gardner trade looks lopsided in favor of the New York Jets, the Dallas Cowboys have seen strong short-term returns from Quinnen Williams.

Williams had a modest showing in the second half of the 2025 season with the Cowboys, but he's recorded 29 tackles (a league-leading 11 for loss), five sacks and 13 pressures in eight games this year. Dallas signed him to a three-year, $105.9 million extension in August, and he's fulfilling the expectations that come with a massive new deal. However, the Cowboys' defense remains one of the league's worst, ranking 27th in points allowed and giving up the most yards per game entering Week 9.

With the Cowboys' 2026 second-rounder, the Jets moved down several spots to select cornerback D'Angelo Ponds and picked up a fourth-rounder, which they used to select quarterback Cade Klubnik. Mazi Smith only played 54 defensive snaps with Gang Green before the team released him.

Assuming the Jets draft a quarterback with one of their three 2027 first-round picks, Klubnik will be a developmental backup at best. However, that Cowboys pick could change the franchise's trajectory, whether it's a quarterback or an immediate-impact starter.

Cowboys Acquire Amari Cooper from the Raiders (2018)

Dallas Cowboys Received: WR Amari Cooper

Los Angeles Rams Received: 2019 1st-round pick

The then-Oakland Raiders hired Jon Gruden as head coach in 2018, and he tore down the roster, trading away stars Khalil Mack and Amari Cooper between September and October that year.

Mack didn't play a snap under Gruden; the Raiders traded him before the season opener. Cooper had a lackluster six-game stretch, catching 22 passes for 280 yards and a touchdown.

Despite that, the Raiders somehow got a first-round pick from the Cowboys for Cooper. In the 2019 draft, they used that pick to select safety Johnathan Abram, whose physicality sometimes bordered on recklessness and drew penalties.

Abram suffered a season-ending shoulder injury in his first NFL game. Under a new regime, the Raiders released him in the final year of his rookie deal. He'll go down as one of the many first-round picks the Raiders have squandered in recent years.

Cooper had an immediate turnaround in Dallas and earned Pro Bowl nods in his first two years there. He eclipsed 1,000 receiving yards in three of his four seasons with the Cowboys and led the team in that category before CeeDee Lamb's ascension in 2021.

In March 2022, Dallas traded Cooper and a 2022 sixth-round pick to the Cleveland Browns for a 2022 fifth-round pick and a 2022 sixth-rounder.

49ers Get Christian McCaffrey from the Panthers (2022)

Carolina Panthers Received: 2023 second-rounder, 2023 third-rounder, 2023 fourth-rounder, 2024 fifth-rounder

San Francisco 49ers Received: RB Christian McCaffrey

Six weeks into the 2022 season, the Carolina Panthers realized they needed to reboot their roster with young talent. That caused them to trade star running back Christian McCaffrey to the San Francisco 49ers in his age-26 campaign.

At the time of the deal, McCaffrey was three years removed from becoming the third player in NFL history to rack up 1,000-plus rushing and receiving yards in the same season. However, he missed 23 games between 2020 and 2021, which likely impacted his trade value.

Subsequently, Carolina traded all four picks in this deal.

The Panthers used the second-rounder in a package deal to secure the No. 1 overall pick in 2023 and drafted quarterback Bryce Young, who's having his best season despite struggles over the last few weeks. They used the Niners' third- and fourth-round picks to trade up to the No. 80 spot in the 2023 draft for linebacker DJ Johnson, who played in 31 total games before they waived him in September 2025. And Carolina packaged the 2024 fifth-round pick with perennial Pro Bowler Brian Burns in a blockbuster trade with the New York Giants.

In the short term, the McCaffrey trade allowed D'Onta Foreman and Chuba Hubbard to lead the Panthers' ground attack. The latter eventually turned his opportunities into a four-year, $33.2 million extension, and he's still the team's lead ball-carrier. Also, after a 1-5 start with McCaffrey, Carolina went 6-5 without him.

Depending on how this season pans out, the Panthers may sign Young to an extension as he's on pace for career highs in multiple passing categories.

The 49ers don't regret this deal, either. McCaffrey is still one of the league's most productive running backs. He has eight rushing touchdowns and is averaging 4.6 yards per carry this season.

Aside from a 13-game absence in the 2024 season, McCaffrey has been mostly healthy in San Francisco, and the 49ers have played in a Super Bowl with him. They've also ranked in the top eight in rushing in three of the past five seasons.

If Young signs a new contract with the Panthers, you can argue this blockbuster deal worked out for both teams in the long term.

49ers Acquire Jimmy Garoppolo from the Patriots (2017)

New England Patriots Received: 2018 second-rounder

San Francisco 49ers Received: QB Jimmy Garoppolo

This deal has flown under the radar because it didn't include a first-round pick, an All-Pro player or a perennial Pro Bowler. However, the New England Patriots chose 40-year-old Tom Brady over young Jimmy Garoppolo, his potential successor.

Meanwhile, in his first year with the San Francisco 49ers, head coach Kyle Shanahan needed to stabilize the quarterback position. He started the 2017 campaign with Brian Hoyer, who went back to the Patriots after the 49ers released him.

The 49ers acquired Garoppolo in October 2017, but he didn't start until Week 13. He went on to lead the 49ers to wins in all five of his starts that year.

Garoppolo didn't develop into an elite quarterback, but he was good enough to help lead the 49ers to a Super Bowl and an NFC Championship Game before Brock Purdy took over in 2022. Garoppolo benefitted from playing under Shanahan, one of the league's best play-callers.

Meanwhile, the Patriots used the 49ers' pick in a trade to acquire additional selections.

ESPN's Mike Reiss listed the players whom New England acquired via a series of trades that started with San Francisco's 2018 second-rounder. Among them, running back Damien Harris made the biggest impact, leading the team in rushing in 2020 and 2021, though he played only four seasons in New England.

Jets Get Davante Adams from the Raiders (2024)

Las Vegas Raiders Received: 2025 conditional third-rounder

New York Jets Received: WR Davante Adams

As much as Davante Adams tried to downplay trade rumors , his tenure with the Las Vegas Raiders ran its course in three years.

During the 2022 offseason, the Raiders traded their first- and second-round picks in the 2022 draft to the Green Bay Packers for Adams. In doing so, they reunited him with his collegiate teammate, quarterback Derek Carr.

Former Raiders general manager Dave Ziegler made a power move with winning intentions, but a year later, Las Vegas released Carr and signed Jimmy Garoppolo. After that, Adams grew frustrated with his new quarterback and the losses after eight seasons with Aaron Rodgers on the perennial playoff-contending Packers.

Adams appeared on Up & Adams with Kay Adams , where he was noncommittal about his future with the Raiders. Soon after, Las Vegas traded him to the New York Jets.

The Jets' conditional third-round pick in the deal would've become a second-rounder if Adams earned first- or second-team All-Pro honors, or if he was on Gang Green's active roster in the AFC Championship Game or Super Bowl LIX. However, Adams didn't meet any of those conditions, and the Raiders traded the draft pick to the Seattle Seahawks for quarterback Geno Smith, who had an abysmal 2025 season in Las Vegas.

The Raiders took a logical risk with the pick to address their quarterback situation, but Smith fizzled out after one year.

Ironically, Las Vegas also traded Smith to the Jets, swapping him and a 2026 seventh-round pick for a 2026 sixth-round pick, which was packaged with a fourth-rounder to move up for running back Mike Washington Jr. The rookie tailback has shown promising flashes with explosive runs, and he took over the lead role in Week 8.

Initially, Adams seemed happier playing with Rodgers again in New York, but the Jets released both of them in the 2025 offseason after a disastrous 5-12 campaign. Neither team won this deal as of now, though if Washington continues to handle a significant workload, the Raiders' grade would be upgraded.

Rams Acquire Von Miller from the Broncos (2021)

Denver Broncos Received: EDGE Von Miller

Los Angeles Rams Received: 2022 second-rounder, 2022 third-rounder

In 2021, the Denver Broncos couldn't escape mediocrity, treading water at the bottom of the AFC West.

After sitting out the 2020 season with an ankle injury, Von Miller bounced back in his age-32 season. On a slightly lower snap count, he played at a high level, but the Broncos needed to trade assets to revamp their roster.

Denver traded Miller to the Los Angeles Rams, and he helped them win Super Bowl LVI over the Cincinnati Bengals at SoFi Stadium. The Rams added an established edge-rusher who helped solidify their middling defense in the second half of the 2021 campaign.

The Broncos used the Rams' draft picks to select edge-rusher Nik Bonitto in the second round and tight end Greg Dulcich in the third round of the 2022 draft.

Dulcich struggled to stay healthy early in his career and appeared in only 16 games before Denver waived him in November 2024. Meanwhile, Bonitto has blossomed into a Pro Bowler-caliber player. The Broncos signed him to a four-year, $106 million extension in September of last year.

Although the Broncos whiffed on Dulcich, they hit on Bonitto, who's taken the baton from an aging Miller to lead the Broncos' pass rush.

Rams Get Jalen Ramsey from the Jaguars (2019)

Jacksonville Jaguars Received: 2020 first-rounder, 2021 first-rounder, 2021 fourth-rounder

Los Angeles Rams Received: CB Jalen Ramsey

In the 2017 season, the Jacksonville Jaguars advanced to the AFC Championship Game with Jalen Ramsey as a cornerstone All-Pro player in their secondary. He had a lockdown presence with the versatility to line up in the slot.

However, after that campaign, the Jaguars fell to the bottom of the AFC South and needed to shake up the roster with young talent to rebuild.

Jacksonville maxed out Ramsey's trade value, dealing him for three draft picks, including a pair of first-rounders that could've reshaped the roster.

Ramsey earned Pro Bowl nods in all three of his full seasons with the Los Angeles Rams and made first-team All-Pro in two. In his third year with the club, he won a Super Bowl as one of the league's top cornerbacks. Los Angeles made an aggressive move that paid off.

Although the Jaguars capitalized on Ramsey's value, none of the players they drafted with the Rams' picks signed a second deal with them.

Edge-rusher K'Lavon Chaisson struggled to carve out a consistent role in Jacksonville and made a much greater impact with the Las Vegas Raiders, New England Patriots, and now the Washington Commanders.

The Jaguars allowed running back Travis Etienne to sign elsewhere in free agency this past offseason. He eclipsed 1,000 rushing yards in three of his four seasons in Jacksonville but averaged fewer than 3.9 yards per carry in two of those campaigns.

Jacksonville used the 2021 fourth-rounder on outside linebacker Jordan Smith, who appeared in just two games and logged one tackle.

Los Angeles won the deal, while Jacksonville's attempt to retool its roster with the Rams' picks fell flat.

Steelers Acquire Minkah Fitzpatrick from the Dolphins (2019)

Miami Dolphins Received: 2020 first-rounder, 2020 fifth-rounder, 2021 sixth-rounder

Pittsburgh Steelers Received: S Minkah Fitzpatrick, 2020 fourth-rounder, 2021 seventh-rounder

In a shocking move, the Miami Dolphins traded Minkah Fitzpatrick in only his second year with the team. But if you dig into the news clippings from before the 2019 trade deadline, you'll understand what sparked the deal.

After a solid rookie season with the Dolphins in which he logged 80 tackles (two for loss), nine pass breakups,and two interceptions, Fitzpatrick grew frustrated with his role under a new coaching regime under Brian Flores.

According to Safid Deen of the Orlando Sentinel , Fitzpatrick discussed his role with Flores and wanted out of Miami. Soon after, the Dolphins traded the safety to the Pittsburgh Steelers.

As one of the league's top ball-hawking safeties, Fitzpatrick went on to have six productive years with the Steelers, recording 344 tackles (including six for loss), 45 pass breakups and 18 interceptions, three of which he returned for touchdowns.

Pittsburgh used the 2020 fourth-round pick to select guard Kevin Dotson, who played in 39 games (30 starts) before the team traded him to the Los Angeles Rams in August 2023. The Steelers selected cornerback Tre Norwood with the 2021 seventh-rounder. He suited up for 32 outings (including six starts) while logging 61 tackles (four for loss), four pass breakups and an interception.

With the Steelers' 2020 first-rounder, the Dolphins selected Austin Jackson, who's had one solid season at right tackle after transitioning from left tackle. He's survived multiple coaching regimes and remains a starter at right tackle. The seventh-year pro has an extensive injury history that slowed his early development.

Miami didn't get much out of 2020 fifth-round defensive end Jason Strowbridge. He only played 55 defensive snaps with the club.

The Dolphins traded the 2021 sixth-rounder to the Kansas City Chiefs for running back DeAndre Washington and a 2021 seventh-rounder. They swapped that seventh-rounder with a Washington Commanders seventh-rounder and selected running back Gerrid Doaks, who didn't play in a regular-season game. Washington appeared in three games with the Dolphins, logging 28 carries for 86 yards and four catches for 28 yards.

The Steelers came out of this deal with the most productive player. They capitalized on Flores and Fitzpatrick not seeing eye to eye on the safety's role.

Vikings Get T.J. Hockenson from the Lions (2022)

Detroit Lions Received: 2023 second-rounder, 2024 third-rounder

Minnesota Vikings Received: TE T.J. Hockenson, 2023 fourth-rounder, 2024 fourth-rounder

The Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions agreed to terms on a rare in-division deal involving a Pro Bowl-caliber player in 2022, making it worth reviewing four years later.

Tight end T.J. Hockenson caught 67 passes for 723 yards and six touchdowns in his second season with the Lions in 2020. However, the No. 8 overall pick's receiving numbers dipped in 2021. Although the Lions exercised the fifth-year option in his rookie contract, they traded him in his fourth year, and he signed a four-year, $68.5 million extension with the Vikings in August 2023.

The Lions avoided the rising cost of Hockenson's services, but they didn't get much production from the players whom they acquired with the draft capital.

Detroit flipped the 2023 second-rounder into more picks, though it ultimately moved down for backup quarterback Hendon Hooker and used the additional picks to move up for third-round defensive lineman Brodric Martin, who played in six career games.

The Lions used the 2024 third-round pick in a package deal to move up for cornerback Terrion Arnold, whom the team released this past offseason while he faced eight felony charges stemming from a robbery and kidnapping in Tampa, Florida. He's currently with the Seattle Seahawks on the commissioner's exempt list. Arnold didn't live up to first-round expectations in Detroit, logging 18 pass breakups and an interception in 24 outings.

Hockenson tore his ACL and MCL late in the 2023 season, but he's otherwise had a productive run in Minnesota, hauling in 278 passes for 2,667 yards and 14 touchdowns in 57 games.

The Vikings used the 2023 fourth-rounder on core special-teamer Jay Ward and included the 2024 fourth-rounder in a move up one spot for quarterback J.J. McCarthy in the following year.

Minnesota traded McCarthy to the New York Giants in September, but the two other players whom the Vikings acquired in the deal remain on the roster in notable roles.

articles.title: Updated NFL Salary Cap Outlook for All 32 Teams Before 2026 NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline is Tuesday, November 10, at 4:00 p.m.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline is Tuesday, November 10, at 4:00 p.m.

For several top teams, it will serve as the final opportunity to upgrade their rosters in any meaningful way before they embark on a championship pursuit.

What is your team's current cap situation and who is the one player who will have the eyes of the NFL watching him?

Jonathan Taylor only had 13 carries Sunday afternoon against the Dallas Cowboys. After the tough loss, the Pro Bowl running back issued a farewell to Indianapolis, the city to which he was drafted in 2020, just in case this latest outing was his last as a member of the Colts organization.

It sure sounds like he is gone. If so, there are several potential landing spots, but few are as mutually beneficial as the Minnesota Vikings.

The Vikings are a potential Super Bowl contender, thanks to a defense averaging 13.3 points per game. Despite having offensive stars such as Kyler Murray under center and one of the best wide receivers in the league, Justin Jefferson, the offense has struggled, making their 6-1 start even more impressive.

Taylor would theoretically open up the offense, forcing the defense to contend with one of the best backs in the league, a quarterback who can take off and run, and an elite receiver who can make any opposing unit pay at any point in the game.

The Vikings are middle-of-the-pack in total rushing yards this season, with only 113.9 per game.

For Taylor, a fresh start in Minnesota would give him a shot at the playoffs for the first time since 2021.

The haul would have to be massive, similar to, if not slightly less than, what San Francisco paid for Christian McCaffrey. For the Vikings, it would give them another asset on their weaker side of the ball. For Taylor, it would represent the start of a new chapter of his career.

Minnesota can afford Taylor, though it would face some salary-cap restrictions next season that could be problematic. Still, he is an upgrade at the position and a potential difference-maker for a team that has the chance to win a loaded NFC.

articles.title: Buying or Selling Latest Rumors Ahead of 2026 NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: As the November 10 NFL trade deadline looms, league insiders, players and fans are glued to their devices for the latest news and transactions. Reporters have been buzzing about playoff-contending teams swinging for the fences, so blockbuster deals could be on the way.
articles.body:
As the November 10 NFL trade deadline looms, league insiders, players and fans are glued to their devices for the latest news and transactions. Reporters have been buzzing about playoff-contending teams swinging for the fences, so blockbuster deals could be on the way.

The Indianapolis Colts are in the trade deadline spotlight, with star running back Jonathan Taylor and ascending wide receiver Josh Downs generating the most buzz. According to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero , the Colts informed quarterback Daniel Jones that they won't trade him.

Most teams in the thick of playoff races will likely be open to moves that fill roster holes and reinforce injury-riddled positions, but of course, it takes two teams to tango on the trade market.

Here are the latest trade rumors ahead of the 2026 deadline, and whether we're buying or selling them.

Chargers Won't Be Trade Deadline Sellers Due to Optics of Giving Up on the Season

Before the Los Angeles Chargers fell to 0-8, ESPN's Adam Schefter provided the scoop on why they'll refuse to trade players before Tuesday's deadline.

"The Chargers don't like the message of giving up on the season," Schefter posted on X. "Calls from rival general managers on Justin Herbert, Ladd McConkey, Khalil Mack and others keep receiving hard nos."

The Chargers are either bluffing or being unreasonably stubborn. They're the worst team in the league and have no realistic shot at the playoffs. Moreover, quarterback Justin Herbert ( finger ) and wideout Ladd McConkey ( back ) are dealing with injuries. The latter didn't play in the previous outing.

Head coach Jim Harbaugh isn't used to losing this much early in a football season, but general manager Joe Hortiz needs to do his job and at least consider offers for players who won't be around beyond 2026.

Although trading players signals surrender in playoff contention this season, it also lets teams refresh the roster and develop young talent for the future.

Despite reports that the Chargers are turning down trade inquiries, it would still be surprising if they didn't move one or two older veterans who may want a change of scenery.

Cowboys Are Not Trading WR George Pickens

The Dallas Cowboys are a disappointing 4-5 team, though their high-powered passing attack gives them a sliver of hope to make a playoff push.

On the Pat McAfee Show , NFL Network's Ian Rapoport relayed a definitive statement on George Pickens' short-term future in Dallas.

"I was told the Dallas Cowboys aren't trading George Pickens," Rapoport said. "As of right now, there's nothing there."

Despite the Cowboys' inconsistencies, they shouldn't be in sell-now mode. They're still in the NFC playoff race—second place in the NFC East. In Week 17, Dallas will host the New York Giants in a game with potential postseason implications.

Even though Pickens isn't as productive as last year, he's still on pace for 78 catches for 1,065 receiving yards, which are numbers for a high-end No. 2 receiver, given that he's sharing targets with five-time Pro Bowler CeeDee Lamb.

If Dallas were to trade Pickens, it would send the wrong message to a team that's still in the thick of division and wild-card playoff races.

Giants Are Serious Suitors for RB Jonathan Taylor

Jonathan Taylor is the biggest known name on the trade market ahead of the deadline. Several teams have likely asked the Indianapolis Colts about the asking price for the two-time rushing-touchdown leader and 2021 rushing champion.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler talked to executives who believe Taylor is worth a second-round pick and additional draft capital, though the NFL insider thinks the Colts might want the "equivalent of a first-round pick."

Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer narrowed the Taylor trade sweepstakes down to three teams, though he highlighted one as being more interested than the other two.

" The Giants, Broncos and Vikings have inquired, and discussed it, and it appears Denver and Minnesota might be a little less inclined to trade for Taylor now. Conversely, the indication I've gotten is that while the Giants aren't offering what Indy wants, they are a serious suitor ."

The Giants could be an aggressive suitor for multiple reasons. They're in the driver's seat in the NFC East, and their lead ball-carrier, Cam Skattebo, missed the previous game with a hamstring injury.

Furthermore, this season, when healthy, Skattebo has had ball-security issues, and the Giants benched him in Week 6. He has four fumbles in seven outings (six starts).

Also, keep in mind that head coach John Harbaugh had workhorse running back Derrick Henry in his last two years with the Baltimore Ravens.

Taylor isn't the physically imposing ball-carrier that Henry is, but the three-time Pro Bowler is a trustworthy running back who can handle a big workload on the ground and help Big Blue establish a physical offensive identity.

Jaguars Are Reluctant to Trade WR Brian Thomas Jr.

At 6-2, the Jacksonville Jaguars will likely be buyers ahead of the deadline, given their need at defensive tackle, with DaVon Hamilton likely out for the season after tearing his quad. The Jaguars also have a trade asset in Brian Thomas Jr., who has generated some buzz.

Head coach Liam Coen hasn't featured Thomas in his offense. He has one 12-yard touchdown catch over the last four weeks, recording just 10 receptions for 117 yards and two touchdowns for the season.

Despite Thomas' minimal role, Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer reported that Jacksonville is hesitant to trade the 2024 Pro Bowler.

" Kansas City had interest in Jacksonville's Brian Thomas Jr., but the Jaguars have been less inclined to sell on the former first-rounder. While he hasn't been statistically productive, and isn't the best fit for Liam Coen's scheme, Thomas brings a downfield element that's really important in keeping defenses honest against the run, and opening things up underneath for Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington ."

Jacksonville isn't utilizing Thomas, so it's hard to believe that opposing teams need to account for him as a downfield threat. The Jaguars may be holding out for the best offer, hoping to get a second-rounder or an early third-round pick.

General managers looking for wide receiver help will likely turn to Thomas if they can't acquire wideout Josh Downs, which may raise the demand for the Jaguars' receiver and spur a deal.

Raiders Could Trade Kirk Cousins for a Third-Round Pick

The Las Vegas Raiders dropped to 4-5 after a loss to the San Francisco 49ers, but they're still technically in the playoff hunt, and their passing attack has kept them in games. Kirk Cousins has thrown for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions.

Las Vegas will face the Seattle Seahawks, who are only one game over .500, the struggling Cleveland Browns, who have lost back-to-back games, the winless Los Angeles Chargers, the Tennessee Titans and the Arizona Cardinals in five of their last eight games.

With those teams on the schedule, the Raiders still have a pathway to the postseason, so don't expect them to trade away key players before the deadline.

However, NFL insider Charles Robinson presented a counterargument with a strong offer for Cousins.

I think Cousins could be had for a price — regardless of a win or loss against the 49ers on Sunday. The price? I think a third-round pick would be too tempting to pass up for Las Vegas. Yes, it's rich. But the Raiders have been placing a lot of value on Cousins' bridge role as No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza patiently grows as an understudy.

Though, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Raiders haven't received inquiries for Cousins and don't want to trade him.

Even with rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza waiting to take over the offense, the Raiders know they have plenty of time to develop him, and they're still trying to win now. Las Vegas could still trade Cousins if it gets a strong offer, though his price may be higher than most expect.

Ravens Aren't Expected to Trade RB Derrick Henry

The Baltimore Ravens are in a downward spiral on a four-game losing streak. They've been outscored by 22 or more points in three of those losses.

To make matters worse, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport said quarterback Lamar Jackson is "likely out for the season." The Ravens started undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano in their Week 9 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars because second-string signal-caller Tyler Huntley is on injured reserve with turf toe.

With all the bad news at quarterback and the blowout losses, ESPN's Dan Graziano floated Derrick Henry's name as a player to watch ahead of the trade deadline.

" As running back names swirl, keep half an eye on Baltimore's Derrick Henry. As mentioned above, the Ravens are down to an injured, undrafted third-string rookie quarterback for Thursday night's game. They will be 4-5 if they lose, with no idea when Lamar Jackson could return. "

The Ravens lost to the Jaguars, but they haven't given up on the season.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Baltimore isn't expected to trade Henry, who is motivated to turn the Ravens' season around.

"I have not mentioned me going anywhere else," Henry said after last Thursday's game. "I'm saying, 'Let's go back to work. Let's try to get better and turn this thing around.'"

Also, Baltimore traded a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick to the Arizona Cardinals for a 2027 fifth-round pick and quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who lost his starting job last week.

The Ravens probably wouldn't make that move if they were going to pivot their focus toward the future. So it doesn't make sense for them to trade their best healthy player, a move that would hamper the offense with a new signal-caller under center.

Titans Would Need a Fifth-Round Pick to Trade WR Calvin Ridley

The Tennessee Titans offense showed signs of improvement in their last two outings, racking up 322 total yards against the Cleveland Browns and a season-high 440 yards against the Cincinnati Bengals. Quarterback Cam Ward threw for a career-high 304 yards in an overtime loss to the Bengals.

Yet Calvin Ridley hasn't contributed to the Titans' offensive strides. He's recorded one 10-yard reception since Week 6 and has just six catches for 91 yards this season. The 31-year-old wideout missed Week 7 with a hip injury.

Yet, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the Titans want a fifth-round pick for Ridley, who hasn't produced much since Tennessee signed him in free agency two years ago.

"Calvin Ridley of the Titans is considered a backup option for teams that miss out on primary WR targets." Fowler speculated. "Word is Tennessee would need something like a fifth-round pick to part with Ridley."

Receiver-needy teams could be aggressive on the trade market as the deadline approaches, but Ridley is more of a desperation option given his lack of production, age and recent injuries. Last season, he missed 10 games and suffered a season-ending leg injury midway through the campaign.

The Titans may take a late-round draft pick if teams are willing to offer anything for Ridley.

Vikings Might Explore QB Options, Pending Monday's Performance

The Minnesota Vikings' Monday Night Football matchup with the Buffalo Bills may be more than a high-stakes game between one-loss teams.

According to NFL insider James Palmer, the game could influence the Vikings' decisions on their quarterback situation ahead of the trade deadline.

The Vikings will get a second look at Carson Wentz, who played in relief of Kyler Murray in the season opener and led the team to a comeback win over the Green Bay Packers, throwing three touchdown passes.

If Wentz performs well, the Vikings may consider him their starter going forward.

However, if Minnesota's aerial attack remains stagnant with Wentz under center, the Vikings should be aggressive in the quarterback trade market.

Regardless of Monday's outcome, the Vikings will be in a tight race for a division title. Every team in the NFC North has at least six wins. Minnesota could quickly fall behind its rivals.

The Vikings can't be complacent with mediocre quarterback play. Wentz has an injury history from early in his career and was banged up last season. Murray has missed extended stretches over the last two years.

Minnesota needs quarterback insurance, whether Murray or Wentz starts for the rest of the season.

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton.

articles.summary: The New York Jets are in the midst of another disappointing season, and a former first-round pick reportedly wants out.
articles.body:
The New York Jets are in the midst of another disappointing season, and a former first-round pick reportedly wants out.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that defensive end Will McDonald IV informed the Jets that he wants to be traded because he is "extremely frustrated with his usage." However, Rapoport added that the Jets "have not engaged in trade talks" with teams that are interested in acquiring the 2023 No. 15 pick, and they "have no plans to."

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported the Jets have been offered a Day 2 pick in the past:

The New York Post 's Brian Costello reported why McDonald requested a trade:

"My understanding is Will McDonald's trade request came after he had multiple conversations with the Jets coaches about an increased role on defense," reported Costello. "Those desired changes have not occurred, as evidenced by his 24 snaps in Kansas City on Sunday, leading McDonald to seek a fresh start with another team. McDonald has been particularly frustrated by the fact that other teams have tried to engage the Jets in trade talks with offers in the 2nd round range and the Jets have refused."

Despite New York's apparent unwillingness to trade McDonald, some of his top landing spots could include the New York Giants, the Dallas Cowboys and the Jacksonville Jaguars if the Jets change their mind.

At 2-7, the Jets are barreling toward a second straight lost season under head coach Aaron Glenn and a 16th straight year without a playoff appearance. Frustrations boiled over in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, with multiple players seen throwing their helmets in anger during the game.

McDonald has played in all nine of New York's games but has only produced 16 total tackles, three sacks, two fumble recoveries and a forced fumble. The 27-year-old has reached the 10-sack mark just once in his four-year NFL career. Rapoport noted that he's unhappy with his role and "wants more opportunities," but he has failed to show improvement despite the addition of 2026 No. 2 pick David Bailey, who leads the team with 7.5 sacks and five forced fumbles as a rookie.

Still, McDonald would be a beneficial addition to teams in need of a pass-rush specialist. It's hard to imagine the Jets trading him within the AFC, but the Jaguars could be desperate enough to improve their subpar defense. Jacksonville already made a major addition by acquiring veteran safety Jessie Bates from the Atlanta Falcons on Monday, so the team could remain aggressive as it tries to solidify itself as one of the top title contenders in the conference.

If the Jets prefer to trade McDonald to an NFC team, their Big Apple counterparts could certainly use a boost. Like the Jags, the Giants are pushing for playoff contention but have just 16 sacks this season, ranking near the bottom of the league. The Cowboys are in a similar boat with just 17 sacks, so they could also use some help with their pass rush.

For now, it sounds like the Jets don't want to give up on McDonald. However, if an offer comes in at the right price, it would be hard for New York to pass up the opportunity to recoup assets in another lost year.

articles.title: Luther Burden III Injured on Hit from Rueben Bain, Latest on Bears WR's Recovery from Concussion
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears escaped with a 27-24 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday Night Football, but they may have lost one of their top offensive players.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears escaped with a 27-24 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday Night Football , but they may have lost one of their top offensive players.

Per Pro Football Talk's Josh Alper , Bears head coach Ben Johnson announced after the win that wide receiver Luther Burden III sustained a concussion when he took a hit from Bucs rookie edge rusher Rueben Bain in the fourth quarter.

The hit by Bain caused Burden to fumble the ball, and Tampa Bay tied the game 24-24 two plays later. However, Chicago managed to survive thanks to a 49-yard drive over the final three minutes that culminated with a game-winning 38-yard field goal by Cairo Santos as time expired.

While Burden wasn't on the field for the game-winning drive, he had already made an impact with game highs of seven catches for 97 yards and a touchdown. The 22-year-old has now reached the end zone in three straight games, and he leads the Bears with 49 receptions, 644 yards and four receiving touchdowns in his breakout sophomore campaign.

Burden is likely to be placed in concussion protocol, but he will have some extra time to recover while Chicago is on a bye in Week 10. The Bears will be back in action on Nov. 22 against the New Orleans Saints.

If Burden is still forced to miss time after the bye, wide receiver Rome Odunze and tight end Colston Loveland will take over as the top targets for star quarterback Caleb Williams in Chicago's passing attack until he's able to return to the lineup.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 10 Rankings, Projections and Waiver-Wire Tips
articles.summary: If you're still seeking out fantasy football content through the first nine weeks of the 2026 NFL season, that should be a good thing.
articles.body:
If you're still seeking out fantasy football content through the first nine weeks of the 2026 NFL season, that should be a good thing.

Ideally, it means you're still somewhere between competitive and contending and therefore have the chance to do something special yet. And if it doesn't mean that, then it means you're a great fantasy league member for running through the tape in a season that hasn't gone according to plan.

Either way, you're looking to put your best foot forward, so let's plot out that path with an early guide to Week 10.

Waiver-wire target: Shedeur Sanders, CLE (vs. HOU)

To be clear, there's no guarantee Sanders will get a second start for Cleveland, since Deshaun Watson cleared the concussion protocol ahead of Sunday's outing. Still, Sanders showed enough in that matchup for quarterback-needy teams to still consider taking a flier by going 19-of-31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns (zero interceptions) and rushing for another 28 yards on 10 attempts.

Projected stats: 20-of-34 for 247 yards, two touchdowns and seven carries for 17 yards

While McGowan's outlook is a bit murky, he might be the priority pickup this week, especially in leagues with early waiver timelines. Jonathan Taylor remains one of the buzzier names on the trade market, so if he's moved by Tuesday's trade deadline, McGowan could conceivably grab hold of this ground game. Even if Taylor stays, though, McGowan could be helpful to have, as he just showed on Sunday (six carries for 45 yards and a touchdown).

articles.body:
One NFL executive floated a dramatic solution for the Dallas Cowboys in the event they move on from coach Brian Schottenheimer.

"The problem there is Jerry's age (84)," the exec told The Athletic's Mike Sando . "So my thought is, that's where you start to circle for Mike Tomlin. Maybe he just relents, much like when he got Bill Parcells, when he kind of gave in to the powerful coach a little bit."

The source went on to cite Tomlin's reputation as a defensive coach and his familiarity with cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who will be a big part of the Dallas secondary if he signs a new contract with the team.

The Cowboys took down the Indianapolis Colts 27-23 in Week 9 but still have a 4-5 record. Their defense remains one of the worst in the NFL as well. If Dallas once again misses the playoffs, then Schottenheimer could be kicked to the curb .

Even if a coaching change happens, a lot of fans will be concerned it's just more of the same. Look no further than the recent comments from team owner Jerry Jones about his beliefs on coaching salaries:

According to Sportico's Kurt Badenhausen , Tomlin was making $16 million a year in what proved to be his final season with the Pittsburgh Steelers. Coaxing him out of the broadcast booth might require a bigger payout than that.

Is Jones prepared to pay Tomlin that much? Mike McCarthy was a proven coach with a Super Bowl title on his resume and he reportedly got just $8 million annually.

There's also the fact that Tomlin would want to exert some authority over how the roster is built.

The 54-year-old would be the most obvious candidate for the Cowboys to target if they need a new coach in the offseason. Recent history suggests the partnership is unlikely to happen.

articles.title: Grading Every Trade from 2026 NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL trade deadline approaches on November 10 at 4 p.m. ET, and it could spur action among teams in the playoff hunt and clubs seeking more draft capital. Some of the hot-topic rumors could come to fruition.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline approaches on November 10 at 4 p.m. ET, and it could spur action among teams in the playoff hunt and clubs seeking more draft capital. Some of the hot-topic rumors could come to fruition.

League insiders have speculated about the trade markets for Jonathan Taylor, Josh Downs, and Brian Thomas Jr., but surprise moves often come down the pipeline.

Stay tuned here with Moe Moton , Gary Davenport , Brent Sobleski and Kris Knox for analysis and grades on all the trade deadline deals.

Lions Acquire S Andre Cisco from the Jets

New York Jets Received: 2028 sixth-round pick

Since Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch's return from a torn Achilles, the Detroit Lions defense has allowed 20 points or fewer to the Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings and Miami Dolphins. Yet they're still tying up loose ends on defense.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Lions are adding Andre Cisco.

Cisco will reinforce the Lions secondary while All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph continues to work his way back from a serious knee injury.

In the first three weeks of the season, Cisco played at least 80 percent of the defensive snaps with the New York Jets. Then, he saw the field for fewer than 10 snaps in the next six outings, logging zero in Weeks 5 and 9.

Cisco had clearly fallen out of the Jets' safety rotation. That said, in nine games with Gang Green, he allowed a 63.5 passer rating when targeted in the passing game. Even though his coverage has been inconsistent as a center field safety, he may be best suited for a limited role in Detroit.

Jaguars Continue to Bolster Defense, Trade for Davon Godchaux

Jacksonville Jaguars Received: DT Davon Godchaux

New Orleans Saints Received: Conditional 2028 sixth-round pick

After a move for safety Jessie Bates III, the Jacksonville Jaguars continue to focus on the defense, adding Davon Godchaux.

According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz , the 2028 sixth-round pick to the New Orleans Saints would be upgraded to a 2027 sixth-rounder if the Jaguars acquire one as a compensation pick or through another trade.

Jacksonville needed a run-stopper after losing defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton for the season. Godchaux can fill that void. He's a 6'6", 330-pounder who's logged at least 40 tackles in eight of his first nine seasons.

With two transactions, the Jaguars have addressed their biggest defensive needs with solid to above-average additions. They've been proactive and logical with their pre-deadline moves so far.

After Week 4, Godchaux's snap count dropped below 30 percent in New Orleans, so it's no surprise the Saints dealt him for a late-round pick.

Jaguars Acquire S Jessie Bates III from the Falcons

Atlanta Falcons Received: 2027 second-round pick, 2028 fifth-round pick

Jacksonville Jaguars Received: S Jessie Bates III

The Jacksonville Jaguars made a strong move to strengthen their 22nd-ranked pass defense. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the deal, which should boost the Jaguars' pass coverage.

Bates has been one of the league's top ball hawks, logging 74 pass breakups and 28 interceptions in nine seasons. He's registered at least three interceptions in all but one year and goes to Jacksonville with one for the season.

In Jacksonville, Bates should make an immediate impact in the secondary and provide reliable coverage to a unit that needs a big-play eraser on the back end. The Jaguars paid a hefty price for him, but in his age-29 season, he's still in his prime.

Bates has an expiring contract . So, the Atlanta Falcons managed to get premium draft capital for a player whom they probably weren't going to re-sign next offseason, given his age. While the move hurts the Falcons' pass defense in the short term, the new regime gets a pick it could use to find Bates' long-term replacement.

articles.title: Malik Nabers calls out Fox analyst Greg Olsen over critical in-game comments
articles.summary: Malik Nabers wasn't a fan of the Fox commentary about his body language.
articles.body:
New York Giants wideout Malik Nabers didn't appreciate the way he was portrayed by the Fox broadcast team in Week 9. After the Giants' 19-11 win over the Philadelphia Eagles, Nabers called out Fox analyst Greg Olsen after the former tight end made comments criticizing Nabers' body language.

Nabers' full statement — which has seemingly been deleted from Instagram — read:

"Y'all be trying [sic] create a narrative on me soo bad it's actually crazy!! If you dnt like the way I play the game keep the camera off me!! SIMPLE! "But @gregolsen88 callin me a bad teammate when every team I've been on, there's NOBODY I've played with has said dat bout me is crazy! "My face the same way if I'm havin a good game, bad, winning or losing. If it's a problem. 1. Keep the camera off me. 2. Pray bout it! Simple."

"Y'all be trying [sic] create a narrative on me soo bad it's actually crazy!! If you dnt like the way I play the game keep the camera off me!! SIMPLE!

"But @gregolsen88 callin me a bad teammate when every team I've been on, there's NOBODY I've played with has said dat bout me is crazy!

"My face the same way if I'm havin a good game, bad, winning or losing. If it's a problem. 1. Keep the camera off me. 2. Pray bout it! Simple."

During the broadcast, Olsen responded after his partner, Joe Davis, called out Nabers' poor body language throughout the game. Olsen said, "It's just not good" before making a point about receivers who demand the ball, per ESPN.

"But there is a very fine line between being demanding, being a competitor and all of those great things. That's great. It just can never cross [that line] where it feels like it takes away from the success of your teammates. So when your teammate catches a wide-open touchdown, you need to be the happiest guy on the field. You can't still be worried about your targets. That's the fine line. He's a talented young, really good player. He's just got to keep it in check."

Olsen then criticized Nabers for a missed catch in the end zone later on the broadcast.

At no point did Olsen outright say Nabers was a "bad teammate," a narrative Olsen was adamant about on X on Monday morning. The comments, though, appeared to cross the line with the receiver, who certainly interpreted things that way.

While Nabers was held in check in Week 9, he's been a highly productive receiver most of the year. In his return from ACL surgery, Nabers has 648 yards in eight games. That total ranks 11th in the NFL. He's done that despite playing with three different quarterbacks this season.

articles.title: La NFL vuelve a alucinar con Madrid y el Santiago Bernabéu: "Es una experiencia única en la vida"
articles.standfirst: Entrenadores y jugadores de Bengals y Falcons coinciden, tras el segundo partido de la NFL en España, que el estadio y la ciudad estuvieron a la altura de la mejor liga del mundo
articles.summary: Entrenadores y jugadores de Bengals y Falcons coinciden, tras el segundo partido de la NFL en España, que el estadio y la ciudad estuvieron a la altura de la mejor liga del mundo
articles.body: Un año después del estreno con Dolphins y Commanders, la NFL regresó al Bernabeu y el veredicto en los vestuarios fue casi unánime. Los Cincinnati Bengals se llevaron la victoria ante unos Atlanta Falcons que actuaban como locales, pero, más allá del marcador, ganadores y perdedores salieron del estadio del Real Madrid hablando maravillas del recinto, de la grada y de una semana en Madrid que muchos no olvidarán. Ni siquiera la derrota le quitó la sonrisa a Kevin Stefanski. El entrenador de los Falcons quiso empezar su comparecencia dando las gracias. "La experiencia fue increíble. Me refiero a cómo nos han tratado este país, esta ciudad, el Real Madrid, en fin, hemos sido muy afortunados y bendecidos. Quiero que todos sepan lo agradecido que estoy por esto, por cómo nos han tratado", explicó. El técnico no escatimó en elogios hacia el escenario y la afición: "Creo que este estadio y toda la experiencia fueron de primera categoría, de primera clase, lo que sea. Los aficionados fueron increíbles. Me parecieron increíbles durante toda la semana. Así que la experiencia y la del día del partido fueron excepcionales". Su quarterback, Michael Penix Jr., dejó una de las frases de la tarde al situar el Bernabeu solo por detrás de su propia casa, el Mercedes-Benz Stadium de Atlanta: "Después del Benz, es el mejor estadio. Es impresionante. Era un estadio precioso. Fue genial poder jugar allí. Es un estadio precioso, precioso, precioso". En el lado ganador, Zac Taylor también se rindió al coliseo blanco. "Impresionante. El público fue increíble. Estar en ese estadio es una experiencia única en la vida", resumió el entrenador de los Bengals, que solo encontró un pero en toda la organización: "Todos los involucrados en este partido aquí en Madrid hicieron un trabajo excelente, tratándonos de maravilla y solucionando cualquier imprevisto. Salvo por el apagón durante una jugada, creo que todo estuvo muy bien organizado. Nadie más ha formado parte de esto, así que es genial poder decir que nosotros también lo hemos sido". Taylor, además, dejó la puerta abierta a repetir: "Lo estamos pasando genial aquí en Madrid. Sin duda volveríamos si quisieran recibirnos para un partido. Una experiencia fantástica. Creo que es una gran primera impresión para todos nosotros en Madrid, España". Joe Burrow, líder de la ofensiva de Cincinnati, disfrutó del espectáculo tanto como el público: "Me siento genial. Me encantó jugar en este estadio. El ambiente es fantástico. Disfruté mucho ofreciendo un buen espectáculo para la gente de España y me alegró estar aquí". La semana en Madrid también dejó huella fuera del césped. Ja'Marr Chase se quedó con la gastronomía: "Lo que más recuerdo de cuando estuve aquí con mi familia fue la comida. Mi familia es de Nueva Orleans, así que le damos mucha importancia a la comida. Así que fuimos a cuatro o cinco restaurantes para asegurarnos". Su compañero Tee Higgins prefirió mirar hacia arriba: "Aprendí muchas cosas, pero puedo decirte que lo que más me gustó fue la arquitectura de los edificios. Fue realmente impresionante. Luego fui al Templo de Debod y vi la puesta de sol. Ese fue, sin duda, uno de mis recuerdos favoritos de este lugar". Para Barrett Carter el partido tuvo un sabor especial por partida doble, ya que se medía al equipo de su ciudad natal. "Fue muy divertido jugar aquí. Sé que tenemos la mejor afición del mundo, pero venir a Madrid es un viaje largo. Fue especial ver su apoyo y cómo se presentaron; nos animaron con mucha fuerza", destacó el linebacker de los Bengals, que también tuvo palabras para el anfitrión: "Agradezco mucho que el Real Madrid nos recibiera con los brazos abiertos, permitiéndonos adaptarnos a su cultura". Y cerró con una conclusión que resume el sentir de toda la expedición: "Madrid es un lugar precioso, y me alegra que hayamos podido salir a visitarlo y explorarlo. Pero, como dije, cuando tocaba trabajar, trabajábamos. Creo que lo demostramos un poco hoy en el campo".

articles.title: Week 10 Waiver Wire Pickups Highlighted by Audric Estime, Corey Kiner, Seth McGowan
articles.summary: The fantasy football world isn't loaded with intrigue at the moment, but it's absolutely worth a look.
articles.body:
The fantasy football world isn't loaded with intrigue at the moment, but it's absolutely worth a look.

If nothing else, the NFL has likely forced your hand in terms of seeking out roster reinforcements.

The injury bug continues to pester players, as Puka Nacua (knee), Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and Xavier Worthy (hamstring) were among those impacted on Sunday. Throw in a fairly busy bye week in Week 10—Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles and Tampa Bay Buccaneers—and fantasy managers figure to have holes to fill.

Let's try to get those filled with the top-of-mind waiver-wire targets available in 50-plus percent of leagues, per FantasyPros.com .

Audric Estime, RB, New Orleans Saints (7% Rostered)

It was an eventful week for the Saints' backfield and quite possibly the kind that could make Estime one of the better fantasy pickups on the board.

It started with New Orleans claiming Estime after the Cleveland Browns released him. Then, the Saints cleared a path by cutting ties with Kendre Miller. And then New Orleans primed Estime for a revenge game, giving him 15 of the team's 32 carries in its overtime win over Cleveland.

Estime turned those opportunities into 72 yards and a touchdown. Perhaps more importantly, he was clearly the first choice when it came to running back carries. Since quarterback Tyler Shough ran it 10 times, that only left seven carries split between Alvin Kamara (six) and Zamir White (one).

If Estime is suddenly about to be a big part of the Saints' backfield plans, he probably should be part of your fantasy plans, too.

Corey Kiner, RB, New England Patriots (5% Rostered)

For folks searching for season-long stability at running back, Kiner probably isn't the waiver-wire target for you. But for those just worried about Week 10, he might need to top your wish list.

Kiner had been trending up in recent weeks, but his waiver appeal might have less to do with him than it does the situation around him. Because if Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson can't go in Week 10, Kiner could be New England's top back for what should be a high-scoring clash with the Detroit Lions.

The Patriots dug a deep enough hole on Sunday that they couldn't run it much, but when they did, they leaned on Kiner more than anyone. His eight carries were half of the team's total, and his 55 yards were more than half of New England's rushing output. He also had the club's only rushing score.

So, again, while it's hard to say what kind of role he'd handle with this roster at full-strength, he can pretty clearly post some big fantasy numbers if he gets a by-default boost atop the depth chart.

Seth McGowan, RB, Indianapolis Colts (19% Rostered)

For leagues with early waiver periods, McGowan probably has to be the priority pickup. Because if the Colts wind up trading Jonathan Taylor ahead of Tuesday's deadline, that could clear McGowan for RB1 duties the rest of the way.

Even if Taylor isn't moved, though, McGowan could offer some standalone value as a depth piece and spot-starter.

The Colts have given him five-plus touches in the past five games. Two weeks back, he handled a dozen touches (11 carries and a catch). On Sunday, the number was seven (six rushes, one reception), and he had 42 scrimmage yards and his first NFL touchdown.

If nothing else, Indy seems interested in using the rookie seventh-rounder as its change-of-pace running back. And the less it has to play for down the stretch, the more it might want to look his way.
