articles.title: New Eagles Trade Rumors on Jalen Carter and Moro Ojomo After Loss to Giants Ahead of NFL Deadline
articles.summary: As the Philadelphia Eagles continue to flounder amidst a seven-game losing streak, trade buzz continues to circle the team, namely around the team's talented defensive line.
articles.body:
As the Philadelphia Eagles continue to flounder amidst a seven-game losing streak, trade buzz continues to circle the team, namely around the team's talented defensive line.

According to Albert Breer of SI.com, "The Eagles' reluctance to deal Moro Ojomo, and buzz that they want to eventually sign him long term, has people in the league wondering if they'd eventually trade Jalen Carter. At this point, it's just speculation. But there's good logic there, too (they're already paying two guys, Carter and Jordan Davis, at Ojomo's position)."

It's pretty hard to imagine the Eagles trading Carter, especially after signing him to a four-year, $152 million extension over the summer. The two-time Pro Bowler and one-time Super Bowl champion remains a disruptive force, posting 25 tackles (seven for loss), five sacks, three quarterback hits, four forced fumbles and three passes defensed.

Plus he's only 25, and Howie Roseman has rarely been in the business of trading franchise pillars during their prime years.

The 25-year-old Ojomo, meanwhile, is in the final year of his rookie contract and has continued to progress nicely. While he doesn't have the counting stats of Carter (24 tackles, four for loss, five quarterback hits, no sacks), keeping him would obviously be ideal.

It would be a lot of resources to dedicate to the interior of the defensive line, with Carter and Davis already on big contracts, though the Birds often play the trio together in Vic Fangio's scheme.

The Eagles are mired in a 2-7 season, but it's hard to imagine Roseman selling off younger pieces of the core. Given the injury issues the team has faced—and some very real questions about head coach Nick Sirianni—the Eagles seem more likely to undergo a retooling in the offseason rather than a full-on rebuild. In that regard, trading Carter makes absolutely no sense. Trading Ojomo seems more likely, though it would only really be logical if the Birds don't feel as though they have an avenue to re-sign him.

Given some of the lucrative long-term extensions on the horizon for players like Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean, it's possible that Ojomo will have bigger offers elsewhere. But for now, it sounds like the Eagles aren't willing to move the young defensive lineman.

articles.title: Patriots' Mike Vrabel Talks Tom Brady Relationship After Comments Leading Up to Packers Game
articles.summary: New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel caused a stir with his comments about former teammate Tom Brady ahead of Sunday's loss to the Green Bay Packers, but he isn't concerned about the public perception.
articles.body:
New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel caused a stir with his comments about former teammate Tom Brady ahead of Sunday's loss to the Green Bay Packers, but he isn't concerned about the public perception.

Vrabel appeared to indicate some iciness between him and Brady when he told reporters last week that he was "required contractually to catch up with him at some point." However, he clarified his relationship with Brady on Monday.

"I talk to Tom," Vrabel said during his radio appearance on WEEI (15:20 mark). "You guys take everything I say at face value."

Brady, who won six of his seven career Super Bowls with the Patriots, returned to New England as a Fox broadcaster for Sunday's game against the Packers. Legendary tight end Rob Gronkowski was also on hand to be inducted into the team's Hall of Fame during the game. Unfortunately, their comeback didn't bring any luck to their old franchise, as the Patriots suffered a 45-27 loss in front of their home fans at Gillette Stadium.

Vrabel was a member of three of New England's Super Bowl-winning teams, so it surprised many when he seemed to dismiss the idea of catching up with Brady before Sunday's game.

"I think I'm required contractually to catch up with him at some point," Vrabel said during last week's press conference . "I'm sure it'll be a Zoom. I'm sure they won't show up here; I'm sure it will be on Zoom. Yep, there you go. So yep, contractually I'll be talking to him, and I'm sure I'll see him at Gronk's [Rob Gronkowski] induction on Saturday."

After falling to 5-4, it's understandable that Vrabel is looking to move past the hubbub about his relationship with Brady. The Patriots will have another tough test on Sunday when they face the Detroit Lions (6-2) in the NFL Munich Game.

articles.title: Nick Sirianni Addresses Staff Changes After Eagles' Loss to Giants at Home for 1st Time in 13 Years
articles.summary: Embattled Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni left the door open for potential changes to the coaching staff after the team's losing streak extended to seven games on Sunday.
articles.body:
Embattled Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni left the door open for potential changes to the coaching staff after the team's losing streak extended to seven games on Sunday.

"We'll talk," he told reporters. "Obviously, right now my job is to be there for our guys and to go watch the tape and go look through everything. I'll do anything I can to help this team win football games. I'll look at myself internally first and then go from there. My job is to coach the players and to coach the coaches, and anything I can do to help this team win games, we'll do. Everything can always be on the table, but I don't think you change just to change because that's what your record says that—you've got to look at what's really real and not react to anything else."

If there are changes to Sirianni's staff, it likely would come on the offensive side of the ball. While the Birds have been ravaged by injury—including the loss of quarterback Jalen Hurts for the season—the offensive woes have become a theme during Sirianni's tenure.

Last season, the offense regressed so much throughout the season that offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo was ultimately fired in the offseason, just one year into his tenure. He was replaced by another first-time offensive coordinator, Sean Mannion, who installed a completely new scheme.

But the issues have persisted. Even before Hurts was lost for the year the Birds were struggling on offense. Some of that is down to personnel—the offensive line has again struggled, with the in-season retirement of Lane Johnson only exasperating that issue, while key players like DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks have missed multiple weeks—but some of it is unquestionably scheme and game-planning.

And it has been ugly. Really, really ugly:

There is of course a larger question brewing—just how much longer is Sirianni himself safe? If there are staff changes, will they start with him?

There is the sense in Philadelphia that the Eagles dramatically underachieved last season despite making the playoffs, and that trend has carried over into 2026. There is also a general belief in the city, fair or not, that the team's two Super Bowl trips during Sirianni's tenure coincided with the tenures of two very good offensive coordinators (Shane Steichen, Kellen Moore) who went on to become head coaches.

When the team has promoted in-house at the position or gone with a first-time option (Brian Johnson, Patullo, Mannion) the offense has often regressed. The two constants in both cases have been Sirianni and Hurts.

But the latter is currently hurt and Philly's offense has spiraled even further. That has left Sirianni's status in very real peril. Whether the Birds would make an in-season change at head coach—they are heading into a bye week—remains to be seen. But come the offseason, Sirianni's job status is very much going to be a topic unless he turns this thing around.

articles.title: QB Report Cards for 2026 NFL Week 9
articles.summary: NFL quarterbacks are on the move, both literally and figuratively. The Baltimore Ravens already traded for Jacoby Brissett to fill in for the injured Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. While Brissett got up to speed, undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano took the reins of Baltimore's offense for at least one game. The Indianapolis Colts' Daniel Jones and Las Vegas Raiders' Kirk Cousins have been rumored a potential trade targets before Tuesday's deadline. The Arizona Cardinals' Gardner Minshew II, Cleveland Browns' Shedeur Sanders and Philadelphia Eagles' Joe Milton III moved into their respective starting lineups for the first time this past weekend. The Cincinnati Bengals' Joe Burrow and Green Bay Packers' Jordan Love continue to move up and surpass others amongst this season's the MVP race. All of this movement, potential or otherwise, is exactly why Bleacher Report grades every quarterback performance each week of the NFL season to track how the position changes throughout the campaign.
articles.body:
NFL quarterbacks are on the move, both literally and figuratively. The Baltimore Ravens already traded for Jacoby Brissett to fill in for the injured Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. While Brissett got up to speed, undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano took the reins of Baltimore's offense for at least one game. The Indianapolis Colts' Daniel Jones and Las Vegas Raiders' Kirk Cousins have been rumored a potential trade targets before Tuesday's deadline. The Arizona Cardinals' Gardner Minshew II, Cleveland Browns' Shedeur Sanders and Philadelphia Eagles' Joe Milton III moved into their respective starting lineups for the first time this past weekend. The Cincinnati Bengals' Joe Burrow and Green Bay Packers' Jordan Love continue to move up and surpass others amongst this season's the MVP race. All of this movement, potential or otherwise, is exactly why Bleacher Report grades every quarterback performance each week of the NFL season to track how the position changes throughout the campaign.

The Arizona Cardinals' decision to make a midseason switch at quarterback was only a matter of time. Gardner Minshew II providing a spark when called into a game was another expected outcome. However, Minshew's capabilities when asked to actually start are suspect.

The Seattle Seahawks also had a backup-turned-starter in the lineup. Drew Lock outplayed Minshew. Granted, the Seahawks defense is a completely different animal compared to the Dallas Cowboys unit that Minshew faced a week earlier. Even so, the Cardinals made the move with expectations of getting something different at the game's most important position. Instead, a prepared opponent led to yet another defeat.

Minshew did have his throwing arm and wrist bent back just before halftime. He finished the contest, but the potential injury could open the door for rookie Carson Beck to eventually enter the lineup—whether Minshew is available or not.

Score : 34-17 loss vs. Cincinnati Bengals

Stat Line : 20 of 31 for 162 yards, a touchdown and an interception; three carries for 50 yards

Initially, Michael Penix Jr. provided the Atlanta Falcons offense with boost when he took over as stater in Week 3. The Falcons immediately won two games. Since then, Atlanta lost four of its next five and the warts found within Penix's game have surfaced.

Specifically, the third-year signal-caller has performed horribly when pressured. According to ESPN Research (h/t Marc Raimondi ), Penix has completed 18 percent of his passes when pressured. He completed only one of nine attempts when facing the Cincinnati Bengals' oncoming rush.

"We know what happened on that field. We know that's not who we want to be this season," Penix told reporters . "We have to put that on display if we want to win football games. We have to play our football, and if we do that, we will love the results."

Score : 33-10 loss vs. Jacksonville Jaguars

Stat Line : 10 of 18 for 60 yards and two interceptions

Joe Fagnano made his first career and likely last start of the 2026 season during Thursday Night Football against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Baltimore Ravens indicated exactly how much they wanted to rely on the undrafted free agent when the team's offense opened the contest in a wildcat formation, with Derrick Henry behind center.

The Ravens brought in Jacoby Brissett for a reason, and Fagnano did nothing during a spotlight opportunity for the organization to second-guess its path without Lamar Jackson or Tyler Huntley in the lineup.

"[Brissett is ] going to bring his experience and the time he's spent in the league, I think that will bode well for us," left tackle Ronnie Stanley told reporters . "But there's a lot of things that we need to fix on our end. I don't think anyone can just come in and fix all of the problems."

Stat Line : 28 of 39 for 276 yards, three touchdowns, an interception and a fumble lost

Bryce Young can't help the fact officials replayed a turnover on a previous play after the Carolina Panthers already snapped the ball. The quarterback also can't help the fact his tight end accidentally deflected the ball that turned into a miraculous end-zone interception. He can't even help the fact his left tackle was beaten and the Denver Broncos' Nik Bonitto swiped the ball from behind to create a fumble.

Young did play well enough for the Panthers to earn a fourth-quarter lead only to see it slip away after the game turned on that fateful interception. Despite another setback, the Panthers still technically sit atop the NFC South standings, even with a 3-5 record.

"Yeah, of course, (this) hasn't been the most fun stretch, but we're in the middle of the season," Young told reporters . "There will be ebbs and flows. We always have to have that next play, next day, next week mentality, and I'm super fortunate to be in a locker room like this."

Score : 27-24 win vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Stat Line : 22 of 37 for 279 yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions

The lyrics to Metallica's King Nothing feel appropriate after Caleb Williams' performance Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Then it all crashes down and you break your crown And you point your finger, but there's no one around

The Bears escaped with a victory despite every effort to give away the game. However, the movement to anoint Williams the NFL's next great quarterback may have been a tad premature.

To be fair, Williams has been exceptional for stretches this season. But he made three terrible decisions Sunday that resulted in interceptions. A fourth came off a deflection. How Williams responds coming out of this contest will be the most telling aspect of his potential ascension toward superstardom.

"I'm going to throw until I can't throw anymore," Williams told reporters . "That's how I live. I work my tail off to be in this position. I'll never not throw the ball. I could throw a hundred picks in one game, but if it comes down to it, I'm gonna throw that pass to Colston, or if there's a tighter window I'm going to break it in there."

Stat Line : 24 of 29 for 271 yards and three touchdowns; three carries for seven yards and a score

Joe Burrow understands the assignment. More importantly, he can deliver.

"I wanted to come out and put on a show for everybody and show what the excitement of the NFL can be," Burrow told reporters after playing in his first international game. "And the NFL is really all about the stars and players making big-time plays. And so you saw Ja'Marr Chase, you saw me, you see Tee Higgins, you saw a lot of great players out there doing great things. And hopefully people took notice."

During the league's second-ever game in Madrid, Burrow completed 82.8 percent of his passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns. He ran for another score. In doing so, Burrow became the fifth player in NFL history to produce four touchdowns in a four straight games, according to ESPN Insights .

Score : 23-22 loss vs. New Orleans Saints

Stat Line : 19 of 31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns

The Cleveland Browns followed the same formula Sunday that previously led to a winning record. Against the New Orleans Saints, Shedeur Sanders failed to deliver when it mattered.

Sanders made his first start of the season since Deshaun Watson wasn't cleared from the NFL's concussion protocol until Saturday. Once again, the Browns offense sputtered during the first half. However, Sanders and Co. got things going later in the contest.

Specifically, Sanders provided a different dynamic as a passer compared to Watson. As NFL Researcher noted , the second-year signal-caller completed all three of his deep passes for 154 yards. Comparatively, Watson completed only eight deep passes for 272 yards through the first eight games.

However, Sanders' scramble during the two-point conversion failed to create anything positive.

"Yeah, but all that's on me because I scrambled on that," Sanders told reporters . "... I'd say to even be able to get in that position was amazing and I was truly thankful to get to that point. And the moment never felt big. It always felt the same for me, so that's how I know I'm growing as a person and growing as a quarterback in this league. Yeah, so next time we get in that situation, I will have a better plan on what to do."

Score : 27-23 win vs. Indianapolis Colts

Stat Line : 21 of 34 for 335 yards, two touchdowns and a fumble lost

Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys offense made life extremely difficult on themselves throughout Sunday's contest against the Indianapolis Colts. The Cowboys committed 14 penalties for 153 yards, which allowed the Colts to remain in the contest despite being outgained by 237 yards. When it was all said and done, the Cowboys placed the ball in Prescott's hands and the quarterback delivered.

"At the end of the day, (it's) a win. That's all I'm trying to do. That's all we can control," Prescott told reporters . "Individually, doing your part, trying to be efficient, disciplined and getting to win. And obviously when you're not as clean as you want to be, disciplined as you want to be, you make it tougher on yourself. Sometimes you can overcome it. Sometimes you can't. Today we did. Yeah, don't want them all to be this close, don't want it like that. But I've said it before, if I can get the ball in my hands with an opportunity to win the game, I'll take it that way."

Stat Line : 25 of 37 for 237 yards, two touchdowns and an interception

The Denver Broncos' Captain Comeback did what he almost always does: Lead his team to another victory after trailing in the fourth quarter.

Granted, the Broncos were only down one point entering Sunday's final frame against the Carolina Panthers. Bo Nix and Co. immediately responded with a touchdown drive and didn't need last-minute heroics to secure the team's latest victory.

However, Nix's late-game play is no longer a bug; it's a feature. As CBS Sports' Todd Fuhrman noted , Nix's "9.1 career yards per attempt when down 1-8 pts in fourth quarters is the best in the NFL since 2000" among qualifying quarterbacks. Objectively, Nix is simply a better quarterback when trailing late in games.

"I think we're just comfortable in that moment—when things get close at the end of the game," Nix told reporters . "... I'm just glad we're on this side of winning them and not in a streak of losing them."

Stat Line : 17 of 25 for 170 yards and an interception

For once, the Detroit Lions offense was able to lean on its defense to do the job, thus reducing the pressure placed on Jared Goff and Co. to perform at an elite level.

"We've cleaned a lot up," head coach Dan Campbell said of the defensive performance. "Guys are trusting what they're being taught, they're executing it and with that execution comes confidence." Detroit's defensive improvement came at the right time. After a scorching hot start, Goff threw for under 180 yards in back-to-back games. His touchdown-less performance Sunday was his first since Week 12 of the 2024 campaign. From this point forward, the Lions must do a better job of playing complementary football, especially with an international game next weekend before facing the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' aggressive defense then a big meeting with the Chicago Bears.

Score : 45-27 win vs. New England Patriots

Stat Line : 23 of 29 for 372 yards and three touchdowns

No NFL team has asked its quarterback to shoulder more responsibility this season than the Green Bay Packers, and Jordan Love has responded with resounding success.

Love, who currently leads the league with 2,618 passing yards, has dealt with a rotating offensive line and non-existent ground game for the majority of this season. Yet, the quarterback continues to thrive.

During Sunday's outing against the New England Patriots, Love torched the opposing secondary and was particularly effective when pushing the ball down the field. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Love completed six of eight passes of 20 or more air yards for 235 yards and a touchdown. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden became the first Green Bay teammates since Don Hutson and Andy Uram in 1942 to produce 150 or more receiving yards and at least one touchdown reception in the same game, per NFL Researcher .

"Phenomenal," Golden said of his quarterback. "Just being able to play with a guy like that is a blessing."

Currently, Love should be the first name mentioned as the frontrunner for the 2026 MVP award.

Score : 44-22 win vs. Los Angeles Chargers

Stat Line : 21 of 35 for five touchdowns and an interception; two carries for 20 yards

At this point in the season, CJ Stroud has provided a large enough sample size to show he's the Houston Texans' long-term answer at quarterback. Granted, this pressing question shaped the Texans' past offseason, because the organization didn't know whether Stroud was worthy of a mega-contract extension. Clearly, he is.

With Sunday's five-touchdown performance against the lowly Los Angeles Chargers, Stroud is the only quarterback in the league with at least 2,200 passing yards and 16 touchdown passes yet only two or fewer interceptions. His 104.8 quarterback rating also ranks fifth among quarterbacks with six or more starts.

Plus, Stroud handled business against a winless opponent despite being sick entering the contest.

"I don't know what I had, but was not feeling good," Stroud told reporters . "My teammates really helped me. Just to have that type of performance under the weather a little bit was to me a testament to our team and our resilience."

Stat Line : 20 of 34 for 180 yards, a touchdown and an interception

The Indianapolis Colts are now 2-7 and Sunday's loss ended in a manner that's become all too familiar, with a back-breaking interception thrown by Daniel Jones.

The Dallas Cowboys did everything in their power to hand the Colts a victory. Jones and Co. couldn't capitalize. The quarterback's play is a big reason why the Colts have struggled so mightily.

Last season, Jones' decision-making and ability to orchestrate Shane Steichen's offense were impeccable. His regression this season has been eye-opening. Alec Pierce's absence can't explain away everything.

The Colts simply can't threaten a defense beyond 10 yards down the field. Even when Jones attempts to drive the ball vertically, those passes have little-to-no chance of being completed. The issue doesn't fall entirely on the team's remaining wide receivers, either, not when the team still has Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and tight end Tyler Warren on the roster.

Much like the end of his time with the New York Giants, Jones' confidence appears to be shattered. If an opportunity arises to trade Jones , the Colts should leap at a chance to do so, then see what Anthony Richardson Sr. can do for the rest of the season.

Stat Line : 16 of 26 for 242 yards and a touchdown

In recent weeks, the Jacksonville Jaguars leaned on running back Bhaysul Tuten. However, the Jags' running game didn't get going against the Baltimore Ravens. As a team, Jacksonville averaged 2.6 yards per game during the Thursday night affair.

Instead, Trevor Lawrence was able to shoulder the offense thanks to some precision throws.

"I just think he was very on when it was really a game," head coach Liam Coen said of Lawrence. "When it was mattering and things were going and it's a back-and-forth football game early on, he was extremely sharp, accurate and played, again, a really solid football game for us." Jacksonville's signal-caller entered the past weekend's action with the NFL's highest quarterback rating among qualifiers.

Stat Line : 23 of 31 for 242 yards, two touchdowns and a lost fumble

The Kansas City Chiefs handled the New York Jets and running back Kenneth Walker III got back on track after back-to-back down performances. However, the state of Patrick Mahomes' throwing arm was the primary discussion point coming out of Sunday's victory. Rookie David Bailey bent Mahomes' throwing arm backward and caused a fumble. Miraculously, the quarterback finished the contest despite some obvious discomfort. Though the majority of his passes still remained at or near the line of scrimmage.

"From the stories you hear, whenever you can grab the ball and try to throw it, you can't throw," Mahomes told reporters when asked about a potential elbow injury. "Once I threw the football, I knew it wasn't, hopefully, I haven't done the test yet, it wasn't ligament-type stuff, it was more muscle-type stuff."

Score : 38-17 loss vs. San Francisco 49ers

Stat Line : 22 of 32 for 216 yards, a touchdown and three interceptions

The clock is ticking and its about to strike midnight for Kirk Cousins as the Las Vegas Raiders' starting quarterback.

The Raiders have now lost five of their last six contests. Cousins only added to the team's problems Sunday against the San Francisco 49ers. Head coach Klint Kubiak tried to excuse Cousins plays to a degree by telling reporters , "When you're in position to throw the ball every down, starting in the second quarter, you're going to throw interceptions."

While true, Cousins still threw a pick-six before the game was out of hand. At that point, the third quarter had just started and the Raiders were down 11 points. Maybe the following two interceptions were a bit more excusable, but that one certainly wasn't.

"When you get behind, you try to get it all back in one play, and it's hard to be patient," Cousins said after the contest. "And I just probably needed to stay a little more patient and be okay with not getting it all back at one time."

Los Angeles Chargers: Justin Herbert & DJ Uiagalelei

Stat Line : Herbert, 13 of 23 for 193 yards, a touchdown and an interception; Uiagalelei, two of seven for 24 yards and a touchdown

As if this season couldn't get any worse for Justin Herbert, the Los Angeles Chargers quarterback is now dealing a potential broken finger on his non-throwing hand, which caused him to leave Sunday's contest.

Of course Herbert is banged up after being sacked eight times by the Houston Texans. At this point, the Chargers offense is completely dysfunctional. The group may have finally found the end zone this past weekend, but it was already trailing by 29 points in the fourth quarter.

For all intents and purposes, Los Angeles' season is done after its 0-8 start. The coaching staff is frantic to make changes in any attempt to keep their quarterback upright and healthy. Up until now, that effort has been a complete failure.

"Too many, too many times," Harbaugh said when asked about the sacks. "Making adjustments. Made adjustments at halftime and will continue to do everything in our power to keep him protected."

Score : 20-13 win vs. Washington Commanders

Stat Line : 26 of 43 for 228 yards, a touchdown and an interception

When in doubt, throw it to Puka Nacua. The approach is exactly what Matt Stafford did during the Los Angeles Rams' victory over the Washington Commanders. Nacua caught 14 passes on 19 targets for 150 yards. Comparatively, the rest of the Rams' receivers caught 12 passes in total.

"He was awesome," head coach Sean McVay told reporters . "That's one of the things that we want to be able to show as coaches, is show confidence to come right back to you. He made a bunch of plays. We needed all 14 of those catches."

Stafford should be grateful for Nacua, because the reigning NFL MVP doesn't look like the same quarterback this year. His ability to challenge all three levels of the field is erratic. The Rams just hope the 38-year-old still has enough to make one final push toward a championship.

Stat Line : 13 of 25 for 128 yards and an interception; two carries for seven yards

Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis was hampered due to a groin injury and it became obvious throughout the meeting with the Detroit Lions.

"It was tight today, you could see it," Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley told reporters . "He wasn't quite able to go full speed."

Willis' seven rushing yards limited an already overmatched Miami offense. As a passer, the Dolphins signal-caller struggled. Willis completed 52 percent of his passes for 128 yards. It's the fourth time this season Miami's QB1 failed to throw for at least 200 yards. Even with Sunday's performance, the Lions still left Sunday's action with the game's worst pass defense. Yet Willis and his receivers were incapable of doing more.

Score : 45-27 loss vs. Green Bay Packers

Stat Line : 21 of 38 for 299 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions

Unlike Sunday's counterpart, Jordan Love, the New England Patriots' Drake Maye hasn't been as effective with a subpar surrounding cast. Maye has proven he can take on a lot within the team's offensive scheme. At the same time, he begins to press too much and starts with the hero-ball mentality.

This approach has hurt the Patriots, because Maye continued to struggle against the best opposition. When facing top-10 defenses this season, the Patriots' quarterback tends to become a shrinking violet . Maye made numerous poor decisions Sunday and stared down some of his targets, allowing the Packers' defensive backs to make plays on the ball.

"We haven't had a clean, turnover-free game yet," Maye told reporters . "It starts with me. It's one of the biggest differences between winning and losing football games."

Stat Line : 21 of 35 for 265 yards and a touchdown; 10 carries for 51 yards

Tyler Shough's age was considered a slight during the NFL draft evaluation process. He spent seven seasons at the collegiate level before finally being drafted in the 2025 class. Now, the 27-year-old starting quarterback brings a certain level of maturity to the New Orleans Saints.

"I think there's an emotional stability, an ability to take away all the things that happened in the past and be present in the moment," head coach Kellen Moore told reporters . "And I think Tyler does a phenomenal job of that."

To Moore's point, the Saints started slowly Sunday but scored touchdowns during their final two offensive possessions (excluding a fourth-quarter kneel-down). During those series, Shough completed eight of 11 passes, including the game-winning touchdown to tight end Juwan Johnson.

New York Giants: JJ McCarthy & Jameis Winston

Score : 19-11 win vs. Philadelphia Eagles

Stat Line : McCarthy, 12 of 19 for 127 yards and 22 rushing yards; Winston, six of eight for 71 yards and a touchdown

The New York Giants just keep finding ways to win. The team needed both of its quarterbacks to contribute against the rival Philadelphia Eagles.

JJ McCarthy left the contest after a big hit with what looked to be a hip injury. During McCarthy's absence, Winston led a touchdown drive. McCarthy returned to the field, gutted out the rest of the game and even ran for a first down on 3rd-and-10 to extend a third-quarter drive that resulted in three points.

"It was a big first down and getting it with my legs, by (any) means," McCarthy told reporters . "We were doing whatever we can to win this game, and that was obviously a big play where I needed to step up, and I'm happy we did that." At 5-2-1, the Giants own a solid lead in the NFC East since no other divisional opponents currently claims a winning record. Keep in mind, Jaxson Dart hasn't played since Wee 2 and McCarthy wasn't even on the team until late September. Even so, New York continues to find a way no matter who's behind center.

Score : 35-12 loss vs. Kansas City Chiefs

If these grades hinged on physicality, Geno Smith's tackle after Braelon Allen's second-quarter fumble would have easily earned an 'A+' for the effort . However, these grades are based on an individual's week-to-week abilities to play the quarterback position.

In Smith's case, the Jets have lost four straight games and the squad's performance continues to decline. Garrett Wilson didn't play Sunday due to injury, which created a butterfly effect. The Jets offense lost its explosiveness and relied on receivers creating after short pass attempts. Even so, Smith's 56.3 completion percentage and 165 passing yards were his second-lowest outputs of the season.

"We're frustrated with him... he's been doing very well distributing the ball and leading this offense," running back Breece Hall told reporters . "He definitely deserves for us to play better for him."

Stat Line : 18 of 34 for 169 yards and a fumble lost; nine carries for 64 yards

The Philadelphia Eagles started their third quarterback this season to provide a spark. Also, Tanner McKee was dealing with a cracked rib. Enter Joe Milton III. He fared as well as those who proceeded him, and the Eagles lost their seventh straight game.

Milton, who was starting his first NFL game, faced consistent pressure and wasn't able to unleash the cannon strapped to his right shoulder. Instead, the Eagles' quarterback lead his team with 64 rushing yards. The Giants sacked Milton seven times and hit him on 11 different occasions.

"Man, the Giants played great today," Milton told reporters . "They had a great defensive (effort) and great players over there. What they did today was just pressure and play over top."

Stat Line : 17 of 25 for 232 yards, two touchdowns and an interception; seven carries for 40 yards and a score

Prior to Sunday's meeting with the San Francisco 49ers, Las Vegas Raiders cornerback Eric Stokes said the following about the opposing quarterback, "[Brock] Purdy is having a heck of a season. You just have to know everything that he's doing. He's an on-time quarterback. You've got to be on your P's and Q's."

Subsequently, Purdy completed 68 percent of his passes for 232 yards and two touchdowns. One instance of an imperfect pass led to an underneath defender snatching an interception. Otherwise, the Niners had the game in hand through all four quarters. A caveat does exist within Purdy's game. His scrambling ability can't be overlooked. His 40 rushing yards Sunday were a season-high.

Stat Line : 19 of 28 for 175 yards and a touchdown

Sam Darnold wasn't available Sunday due to a quad injury. Drew Lock re-entered the Seattle Seahawks' starting lineup and continued his outstanding relief performance from earlier this season.

However, Lock also suffered an oblique injury during the game. He played through the pain and finished the contest. Lock's status for next week's contest against the Las Vegas Raiders is questionable. Even if he doesn't play, Seattle's QB2 already helped the Seahawks win three games this season.

"That dude's a beast, man," safety Julian Love said when asked about Lock's performance. "He's so tough. And, just so cool. Nothing fazes him, no matter what. He's confident, he has swagger. He plays offense like a defensive player. I think that's why all of us really love him, especially on defense."

Stat Line : 18 of 32 for 243 yards and two interceptions

Well, Baker Mayfield actually completed a pass this past weekend unlike his previous outing. That's about the only positive coming out of Sunday's primetime matchup against the Chicago Bears.

The Bears kept handing the Buccaneers opportunity after opportunity thanks to five turnovers. Those led to only 10 points. Though a tying touchdown drive came late in the fourth quarter after a Luther Burden fumble. Tampa Bay made its way into the end zone thanks to a couple of Bucky Irving runs.

"We gotta capitalize on [those turnovers]," Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles told reporters . "We gotta score points and we can't give them the ball back."

Mayfield's performance provided more bad than good, specifically a pick-six that gave the Bears an 11-point second-half lead.

Stat Line : 24 of 35 for 274 yards, a touchdown and a fumble lost

Jayden Daniels summed up the Washington Commanders' performance as simply as he could.

"Myles Garrett happened," Daniels told reporters .

Garrett returned from injury to play his second game with the Los Angeles Rams. The reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year terrorized Daniels throughout the contest. Due to continuing issues along the Commanders' offensive line, Garrett dominated and registered three sacks.

To make matters worse, two of Washington's top three wide receivers—not including Terry McLaurin, who's already out for the season—weren't available due to injuries. The Commanders weren't overly effective or committed to running the ball, either. Thus, Daniels had a difficult day, particularly during the second half, which is why Washington's halftime lead disappeared.

articles.title: New Shedeur Sanders Rumors on QB1 Status as Deshaun Watson Recovers from Concussion for Browns
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns are turning back to Deshaun Watson as their starting quarterback for their next game against the Houston Texans, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns are turning back to Deshaun Watson as their starting quarterback for their next game against the Houston Texans, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler .

Cleveland leaned on Shedeur Sanders as the starter for Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints after a concussion limited Watson's availability in practice leading up to the game.

Sanders went 19-of-31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns against New Orleans. A big chunk of his overall output (124 yards) came on a pair of completions to Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion.

The second-year signal-caller wasn't perfect but seemingly did enough to warrant another look. Hall of Fame coach Bill Cowher was among those lobbying on Sanders' behalf:

In addition to what Sanders put on tape in Week 9, Watson didn't make a compelling argument for himself prior to the concussion. In eight starts, he's averaging 225.8 yards per game and has been sacked 33 times.

The three-time Pro Bowler isn't as sharp as he was during his peak with the Houston Texans, and he looks particularly shaky in the face of pressure.

The Browns are in the thick of the AFC playoff race at 5-4, and coach Todd Monken will be operating with that in mind. He sees the team more than anyone else, so he may have enough evidence to justify sticking with Watson.

But immediately benching Sanders doesn't look like a strong endorsement of the young passer, and this might convince even more fans he has no long-term future in Cleveland.

articles.title: Jordon Hudson takes legal action over Bill Belichick’s viral shirtless video after Airbnb hosts’ shocking admission
articles.summary: Jordon Hudson has filed a lawsuit against Elise McDevitt and Craig Nolan over the release of a private video showing her boyfriend, Bill Belichick,
articles.body: Jordon Hudson has filed a lawsuit against Elise McDevitt and Craig Nolan over the release of a private video showing her boyfriend, Bill Belichick, shirtless outside an Airbnb in 2023. Filed in Massachusetts on Friday, November 6, the lawsuit accuses the couple of violating Hudson’s privacy by sharing the footage and revealing personal details about their stay. She is seeking damages and a court order to prevent further disclosures.Why Jordon Hudson is suing over the shirtless Bill Belichick videoAccording to the lawsuit, Hudson booked a four-night stay at McDevitt and Nolan’s Winthrop, Massachusetts, home in June 2023 for herself and Belichick. On their final night, McDevitt allegedly sent Hudson a Ring doorbell video showing the former New England Patriots coach shirtless while moving to and from the property.Hudson said McDevitt also mentioned that she was a Dallas Cowboys fan and asked her to return the parking pass. However, Hudson was concerned about why the video had been recorded and whether it would be shared with anyone else.She allegedly asked McDevitt to delete the footage after checking out, explaining that their privacy was important. McDevitt reportedly replied, “We will delete it from ring, but as you know, unfortunately, videos are never totally deleted.”Hudson claimed she left the property believing the recording and other personal details would remain private. She also gave the Airbnb a five-star review.However, the video appeared on social media a few months later and quickly went viral. The clip also became a subject of jokes during Tom Brady’s live Netflix special and brought public attention to Hudson’s relationship with Belichick, which she had wanted to keep private.Jordon Hudson raises more privacy concerns over airbnb hosts’ podcast appearanceHudson’s lawsuit also describes her later conversations with McDevitt about how the video became public. She claims McDevitt initially denied sharing it, saying, “I absolutely did not leak this video to twitter or anyone.”However, in May 2025, McDevitt allegedly contacted Hudson and admitted that she and Nolan had sent the footage to a few people to check whether the man in it was actually Belichick.According to the complaint, McDevitt said, “We had sent it to a few people initially wondering is this him Mr. Belichick, isn’t it him and I don’t know what happened from there, but we did delete it from the camera, as I assured you.”Hudson became concerned again after McDevitt and Nolan appeared on Pablo Torre’s podcast, Pablo Torre Finds Out. The episode discussed the Ring video and included additional footage. Hudson questioned why they had shared more material with a reporter.She also claims McDevitt sent her hostile messages after Airbnb removed the rental property from its platform following a privacy policy complaint. One alleged message read, “Now that you destroyed our livelihood, we are weighing our options about whom we will talk to and what we will discuss with them.”Hudson is seeking damages, attorney fees and a court order preventing the couple from sharing more private information about her. McDevitt declined to comment when contacted by the California Post.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFL Trade Rumors on Jonathan Taylor, Brian Thomas Jr. and More Predictions on Landing Spots
articles.summary: Transaction time is fully upon us.
articles.body:
The wait for the 2026 NFL trade deadline is effectively down to hours at this point, as the final buzzer will sound on Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET.

A lot could change between now and then, especially if the recent rumor-mill chatter is to be believed. Let's dive into that buzz and use it to predict where the players involved might land.

Giants Out of Jonathan Taylor Sweepstakes?

If the Indianapolis Colts are interested in trading Jonathan Taylor, they might need to scratch one team off of his suitors list.

Per ESPN's Jordan Raanan, "it would be a surprise at this point if Jonathan Taylor is traded to the Giants."

Surprises can, of course, happen, so this hardly torpedoes the possibility. The Giants are proving plenty resilient at 5-2-1, despite struggling to keep their running backs healthy or producing.

But maybe New York feels like it has enough to get by with the ground game as is. Or perhaps it's just not interested in paying a premium for a running back, or doesn't see the wisdom of investing a ton with Jaxson Dart out for the season. Either way, Taylor's potential new home probably isn't the Big Apple.

Prediction: Taylor is traded to the Minnesota Vikings.

For simplicity's sake, trade deadline participants are often thrown into one of two buckets: either as buyers or sellers. Sometimes, though, it makes sense to dabble in both positions.

Could that be the case for the Jacksonville Jaguars? Because while they were responsible for the latest splash by landing playmaking safety Jessie Bates III from the Atlanta Falcons, it hardly sounds like they've ruled out splitting from 2024 first-round pick Brian Thomas Jr.

"Jacksonville has resisted trade overtures so far, but it sounds like they're going to listen before Tuesday," ESPN's Adam Schefter reported.

For whatever reason, Thomas has struggled to build upon his Pro Bowl breakout rookie season and went without a target in Week 9. A fresh start might be exactly what he needs and also exactly what this deadline provides.

Prediction: Thomas gets traded to the Washington Commanders.

The Tennessee Titans aren't necessarily going fire-sale mode, but they're pretty clearly open for business after the Jeffery Simmons swap. And that might mean great news for the losers of the Jonathan Taylor sweepstakes, since veteran Tony Pollard could be a fine consolation prize.

"They have listened on [Pollard]," per SI.com's Albert Breer . "Pollard has drawn interest from teams looking for running back help that don't want to pay the freight for Taylor, and the feeling from those teams is that it would cost at least a fourth-round pick to pry the veteran back from Tennessee."

As someone who isn't running a front office, that sounds...reasonable. Pollard is on pace to produce 1,000 scrimmage yards for the sixth consecutive season, and his 4.5 yards per carry are in near-perfect alignment with his career average (4.6).

Multiple teams could use a running back boost, and either one of them will get Taylor, or he'll stay in Indianapolis. Either way, there should be a market for Pollard at this trade price.

Prediction: Pollard is traded to the New York Giants.

articles.title: Dianna Russini's New NFL Show Revealed, Explains Return After Hiatus from Investigation on Vrabel
articles.summary: Longtime NFL insider Dianna Russini is returning to sports media with BetUS.
articles.body:
Longtime NFL insider Dianna Russini is returning to sports media with BetUS.

Russini will host a weekly live show, The Russini Report , and pen a regular column for the online sportsbook.

"Football has always been my favorite sport to cover, and I've really missed being in the middle of the action, breaking stories and connecting fans to what's happening across the league," she said in the company's announcement .

"I'm excited to get back to reporting on the NFL and bring that passion to BetUS. I want to give fans more than just the headlines, sharing insider perspectives, uncovering the stories behind the biggest moments, and helping audiences better understand the teams, players, and matchups that shape each week."

Russini resigned from her job with The Athletic in April after Page Six published photos of her and New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel at a resort in Sedona, Arizona.

Vrabel took a brief leave from the team around the 2026 NFL draft amid the fallout.

"I understand that there are questions," he told reporters in April. "I take accountability for my actions, and the actions that caused a distraction to the people that I care most about — my family, this football team, the organization and our fans. My previous actions don't meet the standard that I hold myself to. They don't."

Russini, who worked for ESPN prior to her 2023 move to The Athletic, is one of the NFL's most connected insiders. She told People 's Janelle Griffith she continued to hear from people within the league during her hiatus.

"The absolute best part of this situation has been the loyalty the NFL has shown me," she said. "They checked in with me almost daily while I wasn't working to make sure that I was staying connected to football, to check on me as a person and to just see how I was doing."

Russini said her work with BetUS will combine her usual reporting with some of her opinions on the NFL's biggest stories and rumors.

The Russini Report will debut Wednesday.

articles.title: Sam Darnold, Drew Lock Injury Updates Provided by Seahawks HC Ahead of Raiders Game
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold has been ruled out for Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders, head coach Mike Macdonald said on Monday.
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold has been ruled out for Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders, head coach Mike Macdonald said on Monday.

Meanwhile, backup Drew Lock appeared to get good news as looks to recover from an oblique injury suffered on Sunday:

Lock went 19-of-28 for 175 yards, one touchdown and zero interceptions in a 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9.

ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported that "Darnold could attempt to try to return for next Sunday's game in Las Vegas, but the Seahawks also know that they have their bye the following week. By missing the next two games, Darnold could get the chance to rest the next three weeks before the Seahawks play a big divisional Week 12 game in San Francisco against the 49ers."

Darnold has been considered week-to-week but won't be placed on IR, according to Macdonald.

Darnold cracked a rib on the second play of a Nov. 2 loss to the Chicago Bears before suffering the quad injury late in the game, according to Macdonald.

Macdonald clarified it was the quad injury, not the cracked rib, keeping Darnold out of Week 9 action.

Lock had been previously been dealing with an elbow injury but played this past week with Jalen Milroe backing him up against the Cardinals.

Darnold has started seven games for the Seahawks this season, completing 60.2 percent of his passes with 1,478 yards and 10 touchdowns alongside nine interceptions.

Lock started in Weeks 2 and 3 after Darnold suffered a glute injury in his team's season opener. He most recently served as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Bears while Milroe backed up Darnold.

The Seahawks first listed Lock on the injury report as limited with a right forearm issue ahead of a Week 6 loss at the Denver Broncos.

Lock was listed as limited with a right elbow injury the following week before he was ruled out of a Week 7 win over the visiting Kansas City Chiefs.

Macdonald said after the Oct. 25 game the Seahawks didn't yet know the severity of Lock's injury but that it was "best for us right now to try to calm it down the best we can."

Milroe has yet to see game action this season. He took just three snaps across three different contests during his rookie campaign with the Seahawks.

The Seahawks (5-4) are currently deadlocked with the Los Angeles Rams for second in the NFC West behind the San Francisco 49ers (7-1).

"I think they are the AFC favorite for the Super Bowl," the coach said.

FanDuel Sportsbook gives the Jags the fourth-best odds to win the Super Bowl at +850. The latest odds for every team are as follows:

At 6-2 in their second year under head coach Liam Coen, the Jags appear to be clicking on all cylinders. They made a splash ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline by acquiring veteran safety Jessie Bates from the Atlanta Falcons.

"They're the type of playoff-contending team that's dangerous because they're so versatile," the coach told Sando of the Jaguars. "They could beat you in a low-scoring game. articles.title: Titans 'aware' of airport incident involving wideout Calvin Ridley
articles.summary: Calvin Ridley has just six receptions in 2026.
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans wide receiver Calvin Ridley was involved in an undisclosed "incident" at the Nashville airport, the team confirmed Sunday.

The Titans said they were "aware of the incident" involving Ridley, though declined to provide any details on the situation. The Titans did not play in Week 9.

Titans head coach Robert Saleh weighed in on the incident, calling it "unfortunate." He also declined to provide details on what happened with Ridley, referring to it as a "very minor miscommunication." Law enforcement is reportedly involved.

The situation comes just days ahead of the NFL trade deadline. Ridley, who signed a four-year, $92 million deal in 2024, was thought to be a possible trade candidate for the franchise.

He's seemingly fallen out of favor with the team, as multiple other receivers have played more snaps than Ridley during the season. In seven games, Ridley has just six catches for 91 yards.

articles.title: Seahawks rule out QB Sam Darnold for Week 10 vs. Raiders; Drew Lock dealing with oblique injury
articles.summary: Drew Lock is in line to start his second consecutive game for the Seahawks.
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald provided injury updates on the team's quarterbacks to Seattle Sports on Monday and said starter Sam Darnold will miss another week and be out for Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Drew Lock is dealing with an oblique injury and had a "good exam." The team expects it to be an injury it can manage and that Lock will be able to start against Las Vegas.

Darnold missed Seattle's Week 9 win over the Arizona Cardinals with a quad injury and a cracked rib from the team's Week 8 loss to the Chicago Bears. Lock filled in and picked up the oblique issue, but it didn't keep him off the field. Backup quarterback Jalen Milroe warmed up just in case, but Lock stayed in the game.

The win over Arizona moved Seattle to 5-4, and the Seahawks are currently second in the NFC West, trailing the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers.

Darnold has played in seven games this season and has gone 3-4 in those starts. He has thrown for 1,478 yards with 10 touchdowns and 9 interceptions.

Lock has made two starts this year, and Seattle has won both. The backup quarterback has thrown for 597 yards with five touchdowns and no interceptions. He hasn't run much, with just 29 yards on seven carries.

After the Week 10 game against Las Vegas, Seattle has its bye week. Darnold will have time to heal and return for a huge divisional game against the 49ers in Week 12.

articles.title: Jaguars, Saints Make Surprise Trade After Jessie Bates Deal, New NFL Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars are having a busy Monday.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars are having a busy Monday.

Not long after reportedly trading for safety Jessie Bates, the Jags acquired defensive tackle Davon Godchaux from the New Orleans Saints, per multiple reports:

Godchaux, 31, has played for the Miami Dolphins (2017-20), New England Patriots (2021-24), Saints (2025-26) and now the Jaguars in his career, registering 487 career tackles, 5.5 sacks, 23 tackles for loss and 27 quarterback hits.

This season he's posted 15 tackles in eight games (five starts). The stats aren't much, but he'll give the Jaguars another piece to help against the run.

Per Spotrac, the Saints will take on some dead cap as part of the deal, but nothing prohibitive:

The Jaguars are clearly trying to gear up for a Super Bowl run, which makes sense given the team's 6-2 start to the season. The defense has been excellent, giving up just 15.1 points per game (second-best in the NFL) and only 89.3 yards per game on the ground (fifth).

Adding Bates will help bolster a pass defense that has been a bit more vulnerable and should provide more playmaking, though giving up second- and fifth-round picks to land him wasn't cheap:

As for the Saints, the team is 3-5 and remains in something of a rebuild. Monday's move will provide another opportunity to further evaluate some younger players on the defensive line.

Overall it was a trade that made plenty of sense for both sides, though it won't move the needle like some of the prospective deals that could happen before Tuesday's trade deadline.

articles.title: Fernando Mendoza Compares Kirk Cousins to Yoda from 'Star Wars' amid Raiders Trade Rumors
articles.summary: Fernando Mendoza will eventually be the Las Vegas Raiders' starting quarterback. For now, he's firmly leaning into his apprentice role behind Kirk Cousins.
articles.body:
Fernando Mendoza will eventually be the Las Vegas Raiders' starting quarterback. For now, he's firmly leaning into his apprentice role behind Kirk Cousins.

"I love Star Wars ," Mendoza said to The Athletic's Michael Silver . "I think it's like (Cousins is) Master Yoda out there, and I'm trying to get all the information from him. He's playing at an MVP-caliber level, and him being so receptive to me, and answering all my questions, and looking out for me is super special. He's stuck his neck out for me and really helped me along the way."

The Raiders reportedly have no designs on trading Cousins prior to Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET deadline. We may be getting closer to the point where the team is ready to make a change under center, though.

Las Vegas has lost five of its last six games. In Sunday's 38-17 defeat to the San Francisco 49ers, Cousins went 22-of-32 for 216 yards, one touchdown and three interceptions.

Examining the QB situation in late October, ESPN's Ryan McFadden posited Week 14 could be when Mendoza makes his starting debut.

The Raiders are off in the preceding week, so Mendoza would have more time to settle into the role. The team's schedule gets easier over the final month as well.

The 49ers are allowing the eighth-fewest passing yards in the NFL, so that would've been a tough matchup for a rookie quarterback. Prior to the Week 13 bye, Las Vegas also faces off with the Seattle Seahawks and Cleveland Browns, who are second and sixth, respectively, in pass defense.

Holding off until Week 14 to start Mendoza would mean pitting him against the winless Los Angeles Chargers. There isn't a better opportunity for him to get a win and build some confidence.

The No. 1 overall pick is probably eager to finally play some meaningful snaps. Until that happens, he's satisfied to remain the young padawan.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders, Deshaun Watson's Future as QB1 Addressed by NFL Insider After Browns Lose to Saints
articles.summary: Don't close the door on Shedeur Sanders starting again for the Cleveland Browns during the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
Don't close the door on Shedeur Sanders starting again for the Cleveland Browns during the 2026 NFL season.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Monday the team is expected to return to Deshaun Watson as QB1 in Week 10 against the Houston Texans. That outcome aligned with an assessment of the situation by The MMQB's Albert Breer .

"I'm not sure Shedeur Sanders did enough to take Deshaun Watson's job on Sunday," Breer said. "But I think he played well enough that the Browns might want to see him play a couple of games by the end of the year. Especially since the Browns' first-rounders might not be high enough to get a premier quarterback, so they could be in another bridge scenario in 2027."

Sanders didn't perform badly enough to clearly merit a demotion. He went 19-of-31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns in a 23-22 overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints.

The second-year passer didn't play well enough to convince coach Todd Monken, either.

More than anything, the question worth asking is whether the Browns will be any closer to having a long-term plan at quarterback by the offseason if they stick with their current approach.

Watson is a free agent and has performed like a replacement-level QB so far. Through eight starts, he has 1,806 yards, seven touchdowns and three touchdowns along with a 91.2 passer rating and a 40.9 QBR.

Re-signing the three-time Pro Bowler would mean committing to another stopgap solution, one with a limited ceiling.

Sanders, meanwhile, didn't look great as a rookie and hasn't had much time to develop in Year 2. Whatever opinions you had about him coming into the 2024 draft are probably the same right now.

Rolling with Sanders in 2027 wouldn't inspire a ton of confidence on the basis of what he has shown so far.

The Browns will have a hard time selling their fans on a "bridge scenario" when that has been their strategy ever since trading Baker Mayfield in July 2022. They're on pace to have their fifth different leading passer at the end of the year.

Cleveland desperately needs some stability at quarterback or at the very least a blueprint that doesn't operate one year at a time. That may not be in the offing next spring.

articles.title: Grading the trade: Jessie Bates gives Jaguars another playmaker, but value too good for Falcons to pass on
articles.summary: The Jaguars had needs at other spots, but safety was a position they wanted to upgrade. For Atlanta, the return for Bates was too good to pass up.
articles.body:
On Monday morning, the trade winds kicked back up with a significant deal that will send Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates III from the Atlanta Falcons to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Jaguars will give up a 2027 second-round selection and a 2028 fifth-round pick in return.

Bates, 29, made his first Pro Bowl in 2023 and is a three-time second-team All-Pro selection. He has one interception, three forced fumbles and a 36-yard fumble return for a touchdown this season and is entering the final year of a four-year contract he signed with Atlanta.

The Jaguars have now made a significant addition on defense, but perhaps not at the position most expected. Meanwhile, the Falcons are offloading a notable member of the secondary in spite of being half a game out of first place.

Who won Monday's trade? Let's parse through all the details of the deal.

Jaguars add major piece, filling underrated void

Following the injury to the underrated Da'Von Hamilton, it appeared that defensive tackle was the defense's most pressing and immediate need, but GM James Gladstone and head coach Liam Coen have identified another spot that needed filling first.

Safety flew beneath the radar a bit, but with Eric Murray out for the season and Caleb Ransaw currently on injured reserve, it had become a position of some concern for the Jaguars. Not that you'd know it against the likes of the Colts or the Lamar Jackson-less Ravens; the Jaguars looked like one of the best defenses in the NFL these past two games.

But when it comes time to slow down quarterbacks such as Caleb Williams and C.J. Stroud, plus whoever the Jaguars end up facing in the playoffs, it's an entirely different story. In the one game the Jaguars have allowed more than 20 points this season, Stroud and the Texans hung 34 on Jacksonville and beat them.

Bates has a lot of qualities that fit what the Jaguars seek. He's forged a reputation for being one of the league's better center fielders — and he's a ballhawk, too. Although Bates has only one pick this season, he's had multiple interceptions in all but one full season prior. He's also among the league leaders with three forced fumbles in 2026 and has 14 in his nine-year career, including 11 forced fumbles the past three-plus seasons.

The Jaguars quietly have been winning with an excellent turnover margin this season, leading the league at plus-9. In their two losses and the miracle win over the Eagles, the Jaguars were minus-1 in turnovers. This is a clear formula for victory this season, and they're trying to enhance that edge.

It comes at a cost, however. Bates is set to hit free agency, and the Jaguars just forked over a pretty major pick with next year's second-rounder for what could end up being a half-season rental. Re-signing Bates might now be a priority, but they also must pay wide receiver Parker Washington after a breakout campaign, another quality safety in Antonio Johnson, and a few other big pieces along the lines of scrimmage, including Hamilton.

Jacksonville's salary-cap situation is a bit tight right now, with the team currently projected to have less than $5 million in space, via Over the Cap . Two players, Trevor Lawrence and Joshua Hines-Allen, are slated to eat up nearly one-quarter of its cap allotment.

Gladstone cut his teeth under Rams GM Les Snead, and it's clear he's taking a page out of Snead's "F them picks" approach of using draft assets to secure premier players to push for a Super Bowl title. It's a bold approach, the likes of which the Jaguars previously made rarely.

It also comes at a potential cost down the road, yet it's hard not to support the move if you're a Jaguars fan. Bates has been a very reliable player in his career, missing only a handful of games, has been a four-year captain and has maintained a high level of play, even with Atlanta's defensive backslide.

It might take Bates a little time to settle in on defense, but he should be a major addition and could help solidify this secondary by playoff time. They paid up for it, but if this trade ends up helping vault the Jaguars into their first-ever Super Bowl, it could be a home-run type of addition.

Hours later, the Jaguars addressed their DT need by trading with another NFC South team, acquiring Saints DT Davon Godchaux for a late-round 2028 pick. Along with the Bates trade, the Jaguars' defense got better Monday.

Falcons lose in short term, but value was too good

On the surface, no one should bat an eye at a 3-6 team selling off major pieces, especially when those players are set to hit free agency, as Bates is next spring. But the Falcons' situation comes with a caveat: 3-6 puts them a half-game out of first place in the NFC South.

Even still, the Falcons' season has appeared a bit more wayward with each passing week, even after Michael Penix Jr. had given them a lift. There might even have been some realistic buzz even a few weeks ago after Atlanta's win over the 49ers, the first time San Francisco had lost a game.

But the Falcons, who beat the Bills and Rams a year ago, have to know that teams are not judged simply on a few impressive victories. The total package has been poor. Joe Burrow picking apart the Falcons' secondary was just the latest evidence of this team's southward turn, a week after it was humbled in the rain in Tampa.

Even with some impressive pieces, this Falcons team likely wasn't going anywhere significant this season. Bates is the ideal type of asset to trade off in this situation, given his expiring contract and reaching a point in his career where his value might start to depreciate. If the Falcons had no designs on re-signing Bates, then trading him was 100 percent the right call.

Especially given the price. Receiving a second-round pick is darned good value and above what free-agent-to-be safeties would typically earn. This feels like a seller's market, and Matt Ryan and GM Ian Cunningham deserve credit for identifying this value and pulling the trigger.

This now frees snaps for Xavier Watts, Sydney Brown and DeMarcco Hellams, allowing the Falcons enough runway this season to determine which of them belong in future secondaries. Chances are, that's a position they'll have to address in the offseason in some form, but given the draft-pick return, it was well worth it. The Falcons now have extra selections in Rounds 2, 5 6 and 7 next spring, plus all their own original selections, and are expected to receive multiple compensatory picks .

The Falcons currently have the most salary-cap space in the NFL at more than $110 million next spring, and they should have ample flexibility, even while needing to determine whether Penix remains their future and re-signing some of their own players. They took care of two major pieces already in RB Bijan Robinson and WR Drake London, so a lot of the heavy lifting is already done.

This felt like a no-brainer trade for the Falcons, even if they had to take on a little immediate salary with Bates. Getting back a plum draft pick for an expiring contract made it well worth the price.

articles.title: Tom Brady Gives Surprising Prediction for When Raiders Will Win NFL Super Bowl Amid Ownership Stake
articles.summary: Legendary quarterback Tom Brady has never been short on confidence, and he's bringing that same bravado to his role as minority owner of the Las Vegas Raiders.

Legendary quarterback Tom Brady has never been short on confidence, and he's bringing that same bravado to his role as minority owner of the Las Vegas Raiders.

There's a lot of time between now and 2030, so Brady will try to do everything he can to ensure that his prediction comes true.

articles.title: Josh Jacobs Injured, Latest Rumors on Surgery Decision and Packers RB's Timeline to Return
articles.summary: Josh Jacobs made his season debut just three weeks ago, but the Green Bay Packers running back is now dealing with an injury.
articles.body:
Josh Jacobs made his season debut just three weeks ago, but the Green Bay Packers running back is now dealing with an injury.

Jacobs is set to have surgery after suffering a fractured finger during Sunday's win over the New England Patriots and could miss up to three weeks, according to Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports.

Head coach Matt LaFleur and Jacobs both discussed the situation after Sunday's game:

Jacobs had a solid debut last week, rushing for 36 yards and collecting 55 receiving yards and a touchdown through the air before collecting 39 rushing yards, 13 receiving yards and two total touchdowns.

He had just four carries for five yards, along with a fumble, on Sunday before exiting with the injury.

Jacobs started the season on the Commissioner's Exempt List , but he was cleared to play ahead of the Packers' Week 7 matchup against the Detroit Lions.

Jacobs, a first-round pick in 2019, rushed for 1,329 yards and 15 touchdowns in his first year in Green Bay in 2024 before collecting 929 yards and 13 touchdowns in 15 games a year ago.

The Packers are hoping he can return to that version of himself this year, but the injury could end up being a setback.

With Jacobs sidelined, Green Bay will look to Pierre Strong Jr. to carry the load in the meantime. The team's second-string running back, MarShawn Lloyd, is currently out with a knee injury and his status for Week 10 is not yet known.

The Packers have also been linked to Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor ahead of the deadline, and Jacobs' injury might encourage them to make an aggressive offer for the star.

She appeared comfortable in front of the camera, which is not surprising given her past experience in beauty pageants and modeling.However, it was her caption that made the video even more playful. Referring to the famous Victoria’s Secret runway, Hunt wrote, “Not all of us can walk the VS runway, some of us gotta hold it down at my bach.”Her comment was a lighthearted way of bringing some runway humor into her bachelorette celebrations. In an April 8 Instagram post, Gracie opened up about how she and Derek were friends for eight years before they started dating. But He was doing something neither of us could see: shaping us into exactly who the other needed. He wasn’t withholding- He was preparing. His timing isn’t just good. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes' latest injury update brings relief to Chiefs fans after scary Jets moment
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs fans can finally breathe a little easier after Patrick Mahomes' frightening elbow injury against the New York Jets.
articles.body: Kansas City Chiefs fans can finally breathe a little easier after Patrick Mahomes' frightening elbow injury against the New York Jets. The quarterback has received encouraging news following an MRI, but his availability for the upcoming game against the Atlanta Falcons remains uncertain. Mahomes suffered the injury during Sunday's matchup against the Jets on November 8. The Chiefs quarterback took an awkward hit from rookie defensive end David Bailey while attempting a pass, causing his right elbow to bend backward in an uncomfortable position.The moment immediately raised concerns as Mahomes briefly left the field with his arm hanging by his side. However, he managed to return to the game and helped Kansas City secure a 35-12 victory. Now, head coach Andy Reid has provided an encouraging update on his quarterback's condition.Andy Reid provides encouraging Patrick Mahomes injury updateSpeaking to reporters on Monday, Reid revealed that Mahomes' MRI results were more positive than negative."It was more positive news than negative news on Patrick," Reid said.The Chiefs coach also confirmed that Mahomes is currently considered day-to-day as the team monitors his recovery. Reid explained that the quarterback would need some rehabilitation to help reduce the soreness in his elbow. While the initial results have offered some relief, the team is not rushing to make a decision about his playing status. The encouraging news is particularly important for Kansas City, which is approaching a crucial stretch of the NFL season.Patrick Mahomes' MRI reportedly reveals no major damageThe initial concern surrounding Mahomes was the possibility of a more serious elbow injury after the awkward hit. However, the MRI reportedly showed no significant structural damage, with the injury being described as an elbow strain or sprain.That is a major relief for the Chiefs, considering how important Mahomes is to their offense. The quarterback also showed his toughness by returning to Sunday's game despite the discomfort. He finished the contest with 23 completions on 31 attempts for 242 passing yards and two touchdowns. Although the Chiefs managed to get the win, the biggest talking point afterward was naturally Mahomes' health.Will Patrick Mahomes play against the Atlanta Falcons?The biggest question now is whether Mahomes will be ready for Kansas City's Week 10 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, November 15. Reid has not guaranteed that his quarterback will be available, and the Chiefs are expected to monitor his recovery throughout the week.The first official injury report is expected on Wednesday, which should provide a better indication of whether Mahomes can participate in practice. If he is unable to practice fully, backup quarterback Justin Fields could be asked to take on additional preparation.For now, Kansas City has reason to be optimistic after receiving positive MRI news. However, the Chiefs will need to be careful with their franchise quarterback rather than risk making his injury worse. Mahomes avoiding significant structural damage is certainly encouraging, but fans will have to wait for another update before knowing whether he will take the field against Atlanta.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Inside Tom Brady’s sleep, hydration, and recovery habits: The routine he credits for playing until 45
articles.summary: Tom Brady played his last NFL game at 45, an age when most quarterbacks have been retired for a decade.
articles.body: Tom Brady played his last NFL game at 45, an age when most quarterbacks have been retired for a decade. He announced his final retirement on February 1, 2023, after 23 seasons and seven Super Bowl wins. Brady has long credited that run to a daily routine built around sleep, water and recovery rather than training alone. He laid it out in his 2017 book, The TB12 Method, written with his body coach Alex Guerrero. Some of it holds up well under scientific scrutiny. Some of it does not.How Tom Brady’s routine helped him play until 45The numbers are hard to argue with. In 2021, at age 44, Brady led the league with 5,316 passing yards and 43 touchdown passes. He was still taking the field in 2022 at 45, a year after most analysts expected him to slow down. Durability was the story, not just talent.Brady’s own explanation is that availability beats everything. A quarterback who stays healthy for 17 games a year, season after season, builds a career that a more gifted but injured player cannot. So his habits were not about peak performance on one Sunday. They were about being ready on the next one, and the one after that.That thinking explains why his routine looks so ordinary on paper. There is no secret drill. It is a lot of small, repeated choices around rest, fluids and muscle care, made every day for more than two decades.Why sleep came before everything elseBrady has described sleep as the foundation of his recovery. He has said he aims for roughly nine hours a night, which meant early bedtimes that were often reported as around 8:30 pm during the season. For a famous athlete with a busy family life, that is a real sacrifice.He also paid attention to the bedroom itself. He has talked about keeping the room dark and cool and avoiding screens late in the evening. He promoted sleepwear designed to support recovery, but those product claims are marketing, and independent evidence for them is thin.The broader science, though, is on his side. A well-known Stanford study led by researcher Cheri Mah had college basketball players extend their sleep to about ten hours a night. Their sprint times and shooting accuracy improved. Sleep is when the body repairs muscle and consolidates learning, which matters for a quarterback who has to memorize hundreds of plays and read defenses in a split second.The lesson is simple. Brady did not find a trick. He treated sleep as part of his job.The water habit behind the muscle workHydration is the part of the TB12 Method that gets the most attention. Brady’s guideline is to drink at least half your body weight in ounces of water every day, and more when you train hard. He has also used electrolytes to help his body hold on to fluid, and the brand he co-founded sells them.His reasoning is that well-hydrated muscle is more elastic, and elastic muscle is less likely to tear. That idea is partly right. Sports medicine groups agree that losing even about two percent of body weight through sweat can hurt performance and concentration. Staying ahead of thirst is sound advice.The claim that water alone prevents injuries is harder to prove. Most sports scientists would say hydration helps you perform and recover, but it is one factor among many. Brady’s water intake also came alongside a mostly plant-based diet, careful training loads and a medical team, so it is difficult to credit any single piece.For everyday readers, the useful takeaway is modest. Drink steadily through the day, not only when you are parched, and drink more when you sweat.Recovery off the field: pliability, cold and the evidence gapThe third pillar is what Brady and Guerrero call pliability. It means working the muscles with foam rollers, vibrating balls and manual massage so they stay long and soft, not tight and bulky. Brady also leaned on resistance bands and lighter weights instead of heavy lifting. The idea was to build strength without stiffness.Many athletes now do something similar, and physical therapists generally support regular mobility work and soft tissue care. It can ease soreness and help range of motion. That is a real benefit for a player who took hits for 23 years.Other parts of the TB12 approach drew pushback. His strict diet, which cut back on foods like nightshade vegetables and leaned on the idea of an alkaline body, has little backing from nutrition research. Dietitians have also questioned some of the supplement claims. Brady’s methods were not a scientific trial, and he had advantages most people never will, including personal staff, top medical care and elite genetics.That does not make his routine worthless. It means the most credible parts are also the least glamorous: sleep enough, drink water, move your muscles, and be patient with your body.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
