articles.title: Packers RB Josh Jacobs reportedly needs surgery on fractured finger, out up to 3 weeks
articles.summary: Jacobs appeared to sustain the injury when his hand got caught up in an opponent's facemask during a stiff-arm.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs left during the first half of Sunday's 45-27 victory over the New England Patriots with a fractured finger.

Per CBS' Matt Zenitz on Monday, Jacobs will require surgery on his fractured finger and will be sidelined for up to three weeks.

Jacobs appeared to sustain the injury while stiff-arming safety Craig Woodson as his fingers got caught in Woodson's facemask.

Jacobs left for the locker room, then returned to the sideline, where he appeared to have his injured finger wrapped. But he didn't re-enter the game and instead went back to the locker room. A committee of Packers backs handled carries in his absence.

The Packers listed him as questionable for the remainder of the game but he didn't return. Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur said afterward that Jacobs had fractured his finger and the team hopes to find a way for him to play with the injury going forward.

Jacobs returned to the lineup in Week 7 in a loss to the Lions after sitting six games on the commissioner's exempt list due to an offseason arrest for an alleged domestic incident . He pleaded no contest to charges of battery and criminal damage to property in September.

In two games since his return prior to Sunday's game, Jacobs has tallied 75 rushing yards and one touchdown on 2.3 yards per carry and 11 catches for 68 yards and two more touchdowns.

articles.title: New stat shows historically bad game for Patriots' Christian Gonzalez
articles.summary: Patriots star cornerback Christian Gonzalez had no answers for Packers receivers Matthew Golden and Christian Watson on Sunday.
articles.body:
New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez had a historically poor performance against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday.

According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Gonzalez allowed Matthew Golden to record seven receptions for 105 yards and Christian Watson to record three receptions for 82 yards when lined up against each of them. He became the only defender since at least 2018 to allow more than 80 receiving yards to two different players in the same game.

Gonzalez was part of a Patriots secondary that had no consistent answers for Packers quarterback Jordan Love and the star receiving duo at his disposal. Love repeatedly unleashed deep shots downfield, taking advantage of coverage breakdowns and giving New England's defense little opportunity to respond.

New England struggled to contain Green Bay's passing attack throughout the contest, and Gonzalez did not provide his customary All-Pro-level production to weather the storm.

Watson recorded seven catches for 171 yards and a touchdown while Golden finished with 10 receptions for 164 yards and a touchdown. Together, the receivers accounted for 335 yards and two touchdowns in the game and 187 yards on Gonzalez.

The veteran Gonzalez will look to rebound from this performance in Week 10 when the Patriots take on the Detroit Lions.

articles.title: Terry Bradshaw jokes Fox colleagues disrespected the military by not wearing a tie
articles.summary: Terry Bradshaw is all fun and games on TV except when it comes to being in front of the military, where apparently, he expects everyone to wear a tie. Fox NF...
articles.body:
Terry Bradshaw is all fun and games on TV except when it comes to being in front of the military, where apparently, he expects everyone to wear a tie.

Fox NFL Sunday continued its annual tradition of honoring Veterans Day with its special "salute to military" edition of the popular pregame show. The elongated two-hour show split its crew with Curt Menefee, Michael Strahan, Charles Woodson and Julian Edelman broadcasting from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point, New York, while Terry Bradshaw and Howie Long were live from the U.S. Naval Academy in Annapolis, Maryland.

Near the end of the first hour, Menefee threw the broadcast to Annapolis for Bradshaw's picks, but before giving his winners, the 78-year-old former quarterback took a minute to rant about Edelman and Woodson's attire.

"I'm extremely disappointed in Woody and Julian," Bradshaw said. "They have no respect for the wonderful people there. Howie and I are wearing ties today out of respect to all the wonderful midshipmen. Really, people. You should all just be kicked off the set."

Edelman and Woodson were the only ones not wearing a tie, but they looked great, each with a button-down shirt and sport coat.

Woodson was quick to interject by noting Bradshaw unnecessarily threw them under the bus, saying, "That was low," before defending himself and Edelman by adding, "We're still young."

"It was meant to be low!" Bradshaw fired back.

Howie Long, meanwhile, was standing next to Bradshaw and sought to absolve himself from being involved. "The views of my cohort are not necessarily reflective of my views," Long said.

After Bradshaw settled down enough about the tie to give his picks, Strahan jumped in to defend Edelman and Woodson by taking a shot at his longtime Fox NFL Sunday co-host.

"I'm not sticking up for my guy, it's very hard to listen to a guy wearing suspenders in 2026," Strahan said of Bradshaw, who always wears suspenders.

As a frequent suspender wearer, settle down, Michael. It's a heritage look that fits modern fashion trends. And as someone who frequently goes tieless, settle down, Terry. You can dress nicely without a tie.

It's one thing for Bradshaw to make a joke about something his co-hosts are wearing, or not wearing. But accusing Edelman and Woodson of being disrespectful of the military while they were standing in front of hundreds of military members was an unnecessary low blow.

articles.title: ‘Biggest winner of the night’… Fans rave about Noah Eagle after stepping in for Mike Tirico on SNF
articles.summary: Noah Eagle stepped in for Mike Tirico on Sunday Night Football and earned rave reviews. Mike Tirico stunned NFL fans by announcing he would be absent from NB...
articles.body:
Noah Eagle stepped in for Mike Tirico on Sunday Night Football and earned rave reviews.

Mike Tirico stunned NFL fans by announcing he would be absent from NBC's broadcast of the Chicago Bears against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on SNF.

A statement explained Tirico would not be calling the game because of a health problem. No details were provided on the 59-year-old's exact issue.

NBC filled the void by calling up Noah Eagle to call the game alongside Cris Collinsworth.

Eagle did such a great job that NFL fans are predicting a very bright future for him over the coming decades.

Bears writer Brendan Surgue wrote on X: "Noah Eagle is only 29 and he's already so good. Props to him for coming in at the last minute and not missing a beat.

"He's going to be doing this for another 40 years."

Content creator Zach Cohen posted: "Biggest winner of the night: Noah Eagle.

"A good chunk of us sports fans know he's a great broadcaster, now most of the country does too."

The Athletic's Andrew Marchand added: "Not news but Noah Eagle is very good."

Brandon Carney best summed up the situation, posting: "It's weird not hearing Tirico with Collinsworth but Noah Eagle is so good."

Mike Tirico plans to return to the broadcast booth for Week 10 when the Cincinnati Bengals host the Pittsburgh Steelers in a huge AFC North matchup.

But if he is forced to take any more time off – NBC has learned they are in good hands.

articles.title: Eagles-Steelers game flexed by NFL. See the new kickoff time
articles.summary: If you have tickets to the Eagles-Steelers game, you'll need to get to Lincoln Financial Field earlier.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles schedule got flexed by the NFL on Nov. 9.

The Eagles' Week 10 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Nov. 22 has been moved from 4:25 p.m. to 1 p.m. The game will air on CBS.

The Eagles, who are dealing with a seven-game losing streak, have fallen to 2-7 and last place in the NFC East. Pittsburgh is 6-2 and leading the AFC North.

The game looks like a mismatch and not worthy of a marquee position for the television audience.

The NFL schedule was released in May, long before quarterback Jalen Hurts was lost for the season with clots in both lungs; right tackle Lane Johnson retired; center Cam Jurgens was traded; and wide receiver DeVonta Smith and running back Saquon Barkley were injured.

Flex scheduling provides the NFL a chance to move certain matchups around, particularly in the last several weeks of the season. The Eagles-Steelers matchup isn't an attractive matchup anymore so the NFL moved the game.

Eagles vs. Giants highlights. Top plays from NFL Week 9 matchup

Flex scheduling for "Sunday Night Football" can be used twice between Weeks 5-10 and as needed in Weeks 11-17.

"Monday Night Football" games are eligible for flex scheduling from Weeks 12-17 without limitation.

"Thursday Night Football" games can be flexed up to twice between Weeks 13-17.

Sunday afternoon games that air on CBS or FOX may be moved between the 1 p.m. ET, 4:05 p.m. ET and 4:25 p.m. ET time slots.

The NFL must give at least 12 days' notice to flex any Week 5-13 Sunday night game or Monday night game from Weeks 12-17. Flexing a Sunday night game in Weeks 14-17 requires only six days' notice.

For "Thursday Night Football" Weeks 14-16, flex scheduling should be announced 21 days prior to the game.

Here's a look at the remaining schedule:

Week 11 vs. Pittsburgh, 1 p.m. on Nov. 22 at Lincoln Financial Field: The game was flexed from the 4:25 p.m. marquee time slot to 1 p.m.

Week 12 at Dallas, 4:30 p.m. on Nov. 26 in Arlington, Texas: The Thanksgiving game cannot be flexed. The NFL will have to eat this turkey.

Week 13 at Arizona, 4:05 p.m. on Dec. 6 in Glendale, Arizona: This game should remain at 4:05 p.m. It's not in a marquee slot and is late because the game is in Arizona.

Week 14 vs. Indianapolis, 1 p.m. on Dec. 13 in Philadelphia: The game should remain at 1 p.m.

Week 15 vs. Seattle, 5 p.m. on Dec. 19 in Philadelphia: This is a Saturday game and cannot be flexed.

Week 16 vs. Houston, 8:15 p.m. on Dec. 24 in Philadelphia: This is a Thursday night Christmas Eve game. It could be flexed. It would need to be announced by Dec. 3.

Week 17 at San Francisco, 8:20 p.m. on Jan. 3 in Santa Clara, California: If the Eagles continue to struggle, this game could be flexed. It would need to be announced by Dec. 28.

Week 18 at New York Giants: The time and date of Week 18 games have not been announced to make sure the best games receive marquee placement.

articles.title: Commanders most to blame for Week 9 loss to Rams
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders suffered a tough loss to the Rams. And the boneheaded final play added to the pain. And here are the Commanders who are most to bl...
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders suffered a tough loss to the Rams. And the boneheaded final play added to the pain . And here are the Commanders who are most to blame for the Week 9 loss.

The Commanders fell to 2-5-1 and stand in third place in the NFC East. They are three games behind the first-place Giants in a division where it's likely the only playoff berth goes to the champion.

They were underdogs against the Rams, but put up a decent fight in the 20-13 decision. But who failed?

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Quinn can say what he wants about the final play. He can act like the Rams disguised a zero blitz and forced the hand of Jayden Daniels , according to a post on X by JP Finlay.

"Dan Quinn on the final play of the game says the check down was the option bc of the Rams blitz; said, 'not happy with the execution of that play"

But it's simply not true. It wasn't even a "check down" as Finlay called it. It was a five-step drop and pass. No pass-rush pressure at all. Watch the final play on an X post by NFL.

The Rams rushed five players. Daniels was under zero duress when he threw the pass. Plus, only two receivers went deep. Chig Okonkwo hesitated and ran across the middle of the field. Antonio Williams ran a similar route a little deeper down the field. There appeared to be no plan to throw the ball into the end zone. Any claim otherwise is simply playing mind games and trying to deflect from a defeated decision by either offensive coordinator David Blough or Quinn.

So what Quinn says about the play, according to Sports Illustrated, really doesn't make sense .

"So, there's two plays that you come in," Quinn said. "And so, on the first one, you're taking a shot to the end zone, just like you described. And sometimes, to check for that against a team that does what we call a zero blitz or a max blitz, you want to, 'OK, here's the other play where you can't block them all up.'

"So we got to the second play of what would have been, like, everybody blitzing, check it down and move forward from there. So with eight seconds left, you want two chances at something. And so to not have those, didn't love our execution at our end."

Here's the thing: Quinn gets the blame no matter what. Everything Blough does is on Quinn's plate because Quinn hired him. That's life in the NFL as a head coach. And Quinn should not finish the season in that role. Furthermore, given the way his team has performed this season and last, combined with his Super Bowl debacle with the Falcons, Quinn is probably in his final days as an NFL head coach.

But it wasn't only the final play that Quinn. He also failed to find a way to slow down Puka Nacua. OK, in fairness, many NFL teams struggled to contain Nacua. And the Commanders did get a key interception on a double team of Nacua. But it's the job of a defensive-minded head coach to figure out a way to at least slow down the other team's best weapon. Nacua finished with 14 catches for 150 yards and the game-winning touchdown.

All Quinn can do is try to look ahead with a short week in store against the Giants, according to ESPN.

"All that said, it's a short week," Quinn said. "It's our division leader on the road. And we've got to go. We have to play all three phases together. Seen too much of it where it's part of it, not the whole thing. It has to get right — it has to. We're too far along to not have it all working together."

Sure, Daniels is doing good things. And yes, the Commanders have one of the worst receiving groups in the NFL. Look at this group: Stefon Diggs, Okonkwo, Van Jefferson, Antonio Williams, etc…

And yet, Daniels completed 24 of 35 passes for 274 yards and a touchdown. And no interceptions. Clearly, Daniels gave the Commanders a chance to win the game.

However, how you finish matters. And after his boneheaded play against the Giants that turned a potential win into a tie, Daniels will be scrutinized moving forward. That's especially true this season.

So how did Daniels do when it counted most? Let's look at it. The Commanders got the ball at their own 9-yard line. Daniels hit Diggs for a 42-yard gain. Then Daniels threw an incomplete pass and scrambled for a 1-yard gain.

On third down, he hit Jaden Bradley for a 12-yard gain and a first down. The ball was spiked with eight seconds left. That meant likely two plays available if the first one stopped the clock. But when the next play ended with an incomplete pass, the Commanders had one choice. Chuck it into the end zone for a reasonably short Hail Mary.

That's the only decision Daniels can rightly make in that spot. Instead, he threw the ball five yards down the field. From the 32-yard line. Five yards. There's no worse choice.

It doesn't matter if that was the first read. Daniels had the ball in his hands and had a chance to override the stupidity. He did not. He joined right in line. And the Commanders had next to no chance to score on the final play.

What makes matters worse is that Daniels already has a Hail Mary victory on his resume. Perhaps he believes that is enough.

articles.title: Jared Goff's SI Swimsuit wife had a big Miami weekend, college football gets greedy & Christmas decor time?
articles.summary: Christen Harper celebrated the Lions' win over the Miami Dolphins as the college football playoff expands to 24 teams and drops championship games.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. Well, it happened. My wife pulled the rug out from under me and ripped down all the Halloween decor around the house over the weekend. Didn't even give me warning. No heads-up. I left Friday morning and everything was pumpkins and cobwebs, and by the time I got home late in the afternoon, it may as well have been May. What a punch to the gut. I went to Target later that day, and it was pretty much Santa's workshop in there. Christmas music blaring down every aisle. Reindeer hanging from the ceilings. Ribbons everywhere. And just like that, fall was over — and the holiday season had begun. I held out for as long as I could, but I was ambushed. Now, we're in an undecorated house because the Christmas stuff is in the attic and, frankly, I don't have it in me to go up there quite yet. So, we wait. Perhaps this weekend, when a cold front is supposed to be in town for a few days? An actual cold front. Our first since March! Until then, we're in November purgatory. Sad. NFL WEEK 9 SUNDAY TAKEAWAYS: BENGALS, 49ERS AND PACKERS LOOK SUPER, RAMS FINALLY OVER .500 Welcome to a Monday Nightcaps — the one where Jared Goff's wife, Christen Harper, had a dominant weekend in Miami and helped the Lions to a 19-9 win over my Miami Dolphins. Most ethical tank ever, though. What a pleasure it's been to watch this season! What else? I've got college football officially killing off conference championship weekend, Ron DeSantis (sadly, the outgoing governor of the great state of Florida) weighs in like the PATRIOT he is, and when is an acceptable time to put the Christmas decorations up? You all know where I stand, but I'm curious to see if I'm in the majority or minority here. OK, grab you something to deck your halls (whatever that means), and settle in for a Monday 'Cap! Christen Harper had a big weekend in Miami Big college football Saturday, and a big NFL Sunday yesterday. Let's spin the wheel and start the week with ... The NFL! We'll get to college here in a bit. Crooks. Pretty solid Sunday of football, right? Browns-Saints was a good one. Cowboys-Colts was a mess. The Pats got absolutely steamrolled, which was nice to watch as a Dolphins fan. And my Dolphins ... continued the most ethical tank in NFL history yesterday against the Lions. I've watched a lot of tanks in my 30 years as a Fins fan, and what the fellas are doing this season is a true masterpiece. SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM'S COWBOY HAT MESSAGE HAS FANS TALKING, HOLLY ROWE'S WNBA FINALS PLAN & IS TEXAS' FIELD GRAY? The defense — truly a no-name defense — held the best offense in football to 19 points yesterday. Nineteen! Quick, name ONE person on the Miami defense. You can't. I barely can, and I watch the games! I was a little skeptical coming into this season about how I'd feel week in and week out rooting for a team that just stinks. I've gotta say — it's been a pleasure. Seriously. There is absolutely no pressure on NFL Sundays anymore. None. The team is young, playing well, and losing every game because they just don't have the talent. It's a win-win. I miss watching a winning team, and I miss the feeling of winning a big game. Winning on NFL Sunday is the absolute best feeling as a sports fan. But boy, it's been nice to be stress-free, too. Now, let's check in with Jared Goff's SI Swimsuit wife, Christen Goff (Harper), and get this week started right: Ron DeSantis is right, this playoff format smells fishy "Ended the weekend with a W." Indeed, Christen. You did. Can't argue that. Get us now, NFL, while you still can. The Dolphins are COMING. PS: Shoutout to Jahmyr Gibbs for scoring the game's only touchdown yesterday. I had Gibbs, Ken Walker and George Pickens parlayed for all three to score the first touchdown in their respective games. Walker hit early. Gibbs finally hit in the third quarter (!!!). Pickens never played! Not a bad little payout, which I needed because I got absolutely slaughtered by the books on Saturday. Speaking of college football ... it's official, folks. The playoff will expand to 24 teams next season, and conference title games will be officially eliminated. Thoughts, Mr. Governor? Christmas, Jefferson-Pilot (!!!) & Sophie backs the blue! "A short-sighted move that might bolster profits in the near term but will further erode what has traditionally made college football special," DeSantis posted in response to Monday's official announcement. Thoughts? First impressions? I've said from the beginning that I don't love any of it. Now, I do love more playoff games on actual campuses. That's the biggest issue I have with the current format. Neutral site games are for the birds when it comes to college football. Every single game should be on a college campus. I'll die on that hill. But the elimination of Championship Weekend hurts. I hate it. The first Friday and Saturday of December are unofficial holidays, as far as I'm concerned. Back in the day you'd have the Pac-12 title game on Friday, and the Big 12, SEC, ACC and Big Ten on Saturday — in that order. It was awesome. We have one more dance with it next month, and then it's gone forever. Soak it all in, folks. You will miss it this time next year. I promise. Speaking of missing things, let's rapid-fire this Monday class into a big Monday night of FOOTBALL. First up? This came across my desk today, and I've watched it 50 times already: Today is the 24-year anniversary of LSU's improbable Hail Mary against Kentucky, better known as the Bluegrass Miracle. More importantly ... it was played on Jefferson-Pilot Sports, which is pure nostalgia for kids my age that grew up in the south. Remember Jefferson-Pilot? Man, was it the best. Nothing – and I mean nothing – beat going from College GameDay to whatever third-tier SEC game Jefferson-Pilot was airing at noon. Jay Cutler and Eli Manning had some EPIC showdowns on JP back in the day. It was never the best game, or the best picture quality, or the best announcers. But buddy, it was college football at it's best. That's what they're taking from us! CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP OK, that's it for today. Good start to the week. I leave you with Sophie Cunningham at yesterday's NASCAR finale in Homestead, and a question: When do YOU put up the Christmas decorations? It's been nine days since Halloween. Too early? Too late? What's the cutoff? Let me know! Zach.Dean@OutKick.com. Now, let's have a big week.
